title.zh: 卷一百十三 列傳第一 后妃一
title.raw: 卷一百十三 列傳第一 后妃一 Volume 113 Biographies 1: Empresses and Consorts 1

sentences.zh: 明太祖鑑前代女禍，立綱陳紀，首嚴內教。洪武元年，命儒臣修女誡，諭翰林學士朱升曰：「治天下者，正家為先。正家之道，始於謹夫婦。后妃雖母儀天下，然不可俾預政事。至於嬪嬙之屬，不過備職事，侍巾櫛；恩寵或過，則驕恣犯分，上下失序。歷代宮闈，政由內出，鮮不為禍。惟明主能察於未然，下此多為所惑。卿等其纂女誡及古賢妃事可為法者，使後世子孫知所持守。」升等乃編錄上之。

translations.literal: Ming Taizu, taking warning from the calamities caused by women in former dynasties, established the guiding principles and set out the norms, first making inner instruction strict. In the first year of Hongwu, he ordered Confucian ministers to compile admonitions for women and instructed Hanlin Academician Zhu Sheng: "One who governs the realm puts the ordering of the family first. The way to order the family begins with careful conduct between husband and wife. Although empresses and consorts are maternal models for the realm, they must not be allowed to participate in government affairs. As for concubines and palace women, they merely fill duties and attend towel and comb; if favor and affection go too far, they become arrogant and overstep their rank, and superiors and inferiors lose their order. In the palace courts of past dynasties, when government came out from within, few failed to become disasters. Only an enlightened ruler can perceive it before it happens; those below this are often deluded by it. You should compile admonitions for women and the deeds of worthy consorts of antiquity that can serve as models, so that descendants in later generations know what to uphold." Sheng and the others then compiled and submitted them.
translations.idiomatic: Ming Taizu, taking warning from the damage done by palace women in earlier dynasties, established rules and norms and first made inner instruction strict. In Hongwu year one he ordered Confucian ministers to compile admonitions for women and told Hanlin Academician Zhu Sheng, "One who governs the realm must first order the family. The way to order the family begins with care between husband and wife. Although empresses and consorts serve as maternal models for the realm, they must not be allowed to take part in government. Concubines and palace women merely perform their duties and attend the ruler’s towel and comb; if favor goes too far, they become arrogant and exceed their station, and the order between high and low is lost. In the palace courts of past dynasties, when policy came from within, few cases did not end in disaster. Only an enlightened ruler can see this before it happens; lesser rulers are often deluded by it. Compile admonitions for women and the deeds of worthy consorts of antiquity that can serve as models, so that later descendants know what to uphold." Zhu Sheng and the others then compiled the work and submitted it.

sentences.zh: 五年六月，命禮臣議宮官女職之制。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fifth year, [the emperor] ordered the ceremonial officials to deliberate on the regulations for palace offices and female posts.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the fifth year of his reign, the emperor ordered the Ministry of Rites to deliberate on regulations for palace offices and the duties of palace women.

sentences.zh: 禮臣上言：「周制，后宮設內官以贊內治。

translations.literal: The ceremonial officials submitted memorials, saying: "Under the Zhou system, the inner palace established inner officials to assist inner governance.
translations.idiomatic: The ceremonial officials submitted memorials, saying: "Under the Zhou system, the inner palace established inner officials to assist in domestic governance.

sentences.zh: 漢設內官一十四等，凡數百人。

translations.literal: The Han established inner officials in fourteen grades, altogether several hundred persons.
translations.idiomatic: The Han established fourteen grades of inner officials, numbering several hundred in all.

sentences.zh: 唐設六局二十四司，官凡一百九十人，女史五十餘人，皆選良家女充之。」

translations.literal: The Tang established six bureaus and twenty-four offices; officials altogether one hundred ninety persons, female scribes more than fifty, all selecting daughters of good families to fill the posts."
translations.idiomatic: The Tang established six bureaus and twenty-four offices, with one hundred ninety officials and more than fifty female scribes, all drawn from respectable families."

sentences.zh: 帝以所設過多，命重加裁定。

translations.literal: The emperor, because what was established was excessive, ordered a fresh deliberation and settlement.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor considered these establishments excessive and ordered a fresh revision and settlement of the regulations.

sentences.zh: 於是折衷曩制，立六局一司。

translations.literal: Thereupon balancing past systems, they established six bureaus and one office.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, weighing past precedents, they established six bureaus and one office.

sentences.zh: 局曰尚宮、尚儀、尚服、尚食、尚寢、尚功，司曰宮正，秩皆正六品。

translations.literal: The bureaus were called Director of Palace, Director of Rites, Director of Apparel, Director of Food, Director of Chambers, and Director of Works; the office was called Palace Rectifier; ranks were all regular sixth rank.
translations.idiomatic: The bureaus were titled Director of the Palace, Director of Ceremonies, Director of Wardrobe, Director of Provisions, Director of the Bedchamber, and Director of Works; the office was the Palace Rectifier—all at the regular sixth rank.

sentences.zh: 每局領四司，其屬二十有四，而尚宮總行六局之事。

translations.literal: Each bureau led four offices; subordinates numbered twenty-four; and the Director of Palace overall managed the affairs of the six bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: Each bureau oversaw four sub-offices, twenty-four in all, while the Director of the Palace supervised the affairs of all six bureaus.

sentences.zh: 戒令責罰，則宮正掌之。

translations.literal: Admonitions, ordinances, responsibility, and punishments were handled by the Palace Rectifier.
translations.idiomatic: Admonitions, regulations, and discipline were entrusted to the Palace Rectifier.

sentences.zh: 官七十五人，女史十八人，視唐減百四十餘人，凡以服勞宮寢、祗勤典守而已。

translations.literal: Officials numbered seventy-five persons, female scribes eighteen persons; compared with the Tang, more than one hundred forty were reduced—altogether only to serve at palace chambers and reverently attend canonical custody.
translations.idiomatic: There were seventy-five officials and eighteen female scribes—more than one hundred forty fewer than under the Tang—sufficient only to attend the palace chambers and dutifully maintain routine custody.

sentences.zh: 諸妃位號亦惟取賢、淑、莊、敬、惠、順、康、寧為稱，閨房雍肅，旨寓深遠。

translations.literal: All consort rank titles also took only Worthy, Virtuous, Dignified, Reverent, Gracious, Obedient, Peaceful, and Tranquil as designations; inner chambers were harmonious and solemn, the meaning lodged deep and far.
translations.idiomatic: Consort titles drew only on Virtue, Grace, Dignity, Reverence, Kindness, Obedience, Peace, and Serenity—titles that signified harmony and dignity within the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 又命工部製紅牌，鐫戒諭后妃之詞，懸於宮中。

translations.literal: Again he ordered the Works Ministry to make red plaques, carve admonitory words instructing empresses and consorts, and hang them in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also ordered the Ministry of Works to cast red warning plaques inscribed with admonitions for empresses and consorts, to be hung within the palace.

sentences.zh: 牌用鐵，字飾以金。

translations.literal: The plaques used iron; the characters were ornamented with gold.
translations.idiomatic: The plaques were of iron with characters inlaid in gold.

sentences.zh: 复著令典，自后妃以下至嬪御女史，鉅細衣食之費，金銀幣帛、器用百物之供，皆自尚宮取旨，牒內使監覆奏，移部臣取給焉。

translations.literal: Again it was set forth in statutes: from empresses and consorts down to attendant concubines and female scribes, great and small expenses for clothing and food, supplies of gold, silver, currency silks, utensils, and a hundred kinds of things—all were to obtain instructions from the Director of Palace, memorialize the Inner Palace Directorate for review and memorial, and transfer to ministry officials to obtain and grant.
translations.idiomatic: Statutes further decreed that from the empress and consorts down to attendants and female scribes, every expense for clothing and food, every supply of gold, silver, silks, and utensils had to be authorized by the Director of the Palace, reviewed and reported by the Inner Palace Directorate, and only then issued by the appropriate ministry.

sentences.zh: 若尚宮不及奏，內使監不覆奏，而輒領於部者，論死。

translations.literal: If the Director of Palace did not reach memorial, the Inner Palace Directorate did not review and memorialize, yet one rashly received from the ministries—punishment was death.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who obtained supplies from a ministry without authorization from the Director of the Palace and review by the Inner Palace Directorate was liable to execution.

sentences.zh: 或以私書出外，罪亦如之。

translations.literal: Or if by private letter one sent [word] outside—the crime was likewise the same.
translations.idiomatic: Sending private correspondence outside the palace incurred the same penalty.

sentences.zh: 宮嬪以下有疾，醫者不得入宮，以證取藥。

translations.literal: When palace concubines and below had illness, physicians could not enter the palace; by certificate they obtained medicine.
translations.idiomatic: When palace ladies below the rank of consort fell ill, physicians were not admitted; medicines were procured on written certification.

sentences.zh: 何其慎也！

translations.literal: How cautious it was!
translations.idiomatic: Such was the rigor of these precautions!

sentences.zh: 是以終明之代，宮壼肅清，論者謂其家法之善，超軼漢、唐。

translations.literal: Therefore throughout the Ming age, the inner palace was pure and clear; discussants said its family rules were excellent, surpassing Han and Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Hence throughout the Ming dynasty the inner palace remained orderly and pure; commentators held that its domestic discipline exceeded that of the Han and Tang.

sentences.zh: 爰自孝慈以迄愍后，考厥族里，次其世代，雖所遇不齊，顯晦異致，而凡居正號者並列於篇。

translations.literal: From Xiaoci on to Empress Min, examining their clans and hamlets, arranging their generations—though what they encountered was not uniform, prominence and obscurity had different outcomes—yet all who held the orthodox title are ranked together in this chapter.
translations.idiomatic: From Empress Xiaoci through Empress Min, this chapter lists their lineages and generations in order; though their fortunes varied and their fame rose or fell, all who bore the legitimate title of empress are recorded here.

sentences.zh: 其妃嬪有事實者，亦附見焉。

translations.literal: Their consorts and attendants who had factual deeds are also appended and seen therein.
translations.idiomatic: Consorts and concubines with noteworthy deeds are also included where relevant.

translations.literal: ○ Empresses and consorts, part one
translations.idiomatic: ○ Empresses and Consorts, Part One

sentences.zh: 太祖孝慈高皇后馬氏，宿州人。

translations.literal: Taizu Empress Xiaoci the High, née Ma, was a native of Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xiaoci the Filial and Kind High Empress of Taizu, née Ma, was a native of Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 父馬公，母鄭媼，早卒。

translations.literal: Her father was Lord Ma; her mother was Lady Zheng; both died early.
translations.idiomatic: Her father, Lord Ma, and her mother, Lady Zheng, both died while she was young.

sentences.zh: 馬公素善郭子興，遂以后托子興。

translations.literal: Lord Ma had long been on good terms with Guo Zixing, and so entrusted the empress to Zixing.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Ma had long been on good terms with Guo Zixing and entrusted the future empress to his care.

sentences.zh: 馬公卒，子興育之如己女。

translations.literal: When Lord Ma died, Zixing reared her as his own daughter.
translations.idiomatic: After Lord Ma's death, Zixing raised her as his own daughter.

sentences.zh: 子興奇太祖，以后歸焉。

translations.literal: Zixing marveled at Taizu and gave the empress to him in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Zixing took a keen interest in the Founding Emperor and gave her to him in marriage.

sentences.zh: 后仁慈有智鑑，好書史。

translations.literal: The empress was benevolent and had wise discernment; she loved books and history.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was benevolent and discerning, and devoted to books and history.

sentences.zh: 太祖有劄記，輒命后掌之，倉卒未嘗忘。

translations.literal: Whenever Taizu had memoranda, he would order the empress to keep charge of them; even in haste she never forgot.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the Founding Emperor had memoranda to keep, he entrusted them to the empress, who never misplaced them even in the press of events.

sentences.zh: 子興嘗信讒，疑太祖。

translations.literal: Zixing once believed slander and suspected Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: Zixing once believed slander and grew suspicious of the Founding Emperor.

sentences.zh: 后善事其妻，嫌隙得釋。

translations.literal: The empress treated his wife well, and the rift was dissolved.
translations.idiomatic: The empress won over his wife with kindness, and the estrangement was resolved.

sentences.zh: 太祖既克太平，后率將士妻妾渡江。

translations.literal: After Taizu had taken Taiping, the empress led the generals' wives and concubines across the river.
translations.idiomatic: After the Founding Emperor captured Taiping, the empress led the wives and families of his officers across the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 及居江寧，吳、漢接境，戰無虛日，親緝甲士衣鞋佐軍。

translations.literal: When they dwelt at Jiangning, Wu and Han bordered them; battle had no idle day; she personally stitched soldiers' armor, clothing, and shoes to assist the army.
translations.idiomatic: At Jiangning, with Wu and Han on the borders and fighting nearly every day, she personally stitched armor, clothing, and shoes for the troops.

sentences.zh: 陳友諒寇龍灣，太祖率師御之，后儘發宮中金帛犒士。

translations.literal: When Chen Youliang raided Longwan, Taizu led the army to resist; the empress exhausted the palace's gold and silks to reward the troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Youliang attacked Longwan and the Founding Emperor marched to meet him, the empress distributed all the gold and silks in the palace to reward the soldiers.

sentences.zh: 嘗語太祖，定天下以不殺人為本。

translations.literal: She once told Taizu that to settle the realm one should take not killing people as the foundation.
translations.idiomatic: She once told the Founding Emperor that to secure the realm he should make sparing human life his guiding principle.

sentences.zh: 太祖善之。

translations.literal: Taizu approved of this.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor approved of this counsel.

sentences.zh: 洪武元年正月，太祖即帝位，冊為皇后。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Hongwu, when Taizu assumed the imperial throne, she was enfeoffed as empress.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Hongwu 1, when the Founding Emperor took the throne, she was installed as empress.

sentences.zh: 初，后從帝軍中，值歲大歉，帝又為郭氏所疑，嘗乏食。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the empress followed the emperor in the army, the year suffered great famine; the emperor was again suspected by the Guo clan and once lacked food.
translations.idiomatic: In their early years with the army, a great famine struck; the emperor was under suspicion by the Guo family and sometimes went without food.

sentences.zh: 后竊炊餅，懷以進，肉為焦。

translations.literal: The empress secretly cooked cakes, carried them in her bosom to present; the meat was charred.
translations.idiomatic: The empress secretly cooked flatbread with meat, carried it warm against her body to bring him, and the meat was scorched by the heat.

sentences.zh: 居常貯糗糒脯脩供帝，無所乏絕，而己不宿飽。

translations.literal: She constantly stored dried grain, dried meat, and dried strips to supply the emperor, without any lack; yet she herself did not sleep full.
translations.idiomatic: She always kept dried provisions and cured meats for the emperor so he never went without, while she herself often went to bed hungry.

sentences.zh: 及貴，帝比之「蕪蔞豆粥」，「滹沱麥飯」，每對群臣述后賢，同於唐長孫皇后。

translations.literal: When they became exalted, the emperor compared it to "turnip and bean porridge" and "Hutuo wheat meal"; whenever he faced the ministers he recounted the empress's worth, equaling Tang's Empress Zhangsun.
translations.idiomatic: After they rose to power, the emperor likened those days to the "turnip-and-bean porridge" and "Hutuo wheat meal" of old hardship, and often told his ministers of the empress's virtues, comparing her to Empress Zhangsun of the Tang.

sentences.zh: 退以語后。

translations.literal: He withdrew and told the empress.
translations.idiomatic: When he withdrew, he told the empress what he had said.

sentences.zh: 后曰：「妾聞夫婦相保易，君臣相保難。

translations.literal: The empress said: "Your servant has heard that husband and wife protecting each other is easy; ruler and minister protecting each other is hard.
translations.idiomatic: The empress said: "I have heard that it is easy for husband and wife to stand by each other, but hard for ruler and minister to do so.

sentences.zh: 陛下不忘妾同貧賤，願無忘群臣同艱難。

translations.literal: Your Majesty does not forget your servant's shared poverty and low station; I wish you would not forget the ministers' shared hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has not forgotten our days of poverty; I pray you will not forget the ministers who shared your hardships.

sentences.zh: 且妾何敢比長孫皇后也！」

translations.literal: Moreover, how dare your servant compare herself to Empress Zhangsun!"
translations.idiomatic: And how dare I compare myself to Empress Zhangsun!"

sentences.zh: 后勤於內治，暇則講求古訓。

translations.literal: The empress was diligent in inner governance; in leisure she studied ancient teachings.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was diligent in managing the inner palace and, in her spare time, studied the teachings of antiquity.

sentences.zh: 告六宮，以宋多賢后，命女史錄其家法，朝夕省覽。

translations.literal: She told the Six Palaces that the Song had many worthy empresses and ordered female scribes to record their household rules, morning and evening to examine them.
translations.idiomatic: She told the Six Palaces that the Song had produced many worthy empresses and ordered female scribes to copy their household rules for daily study.

sentences.zh: 或言宋過仁厚，后曰：「過仁厚，不愈於刻薄乎？」

translations.literal: Someone said the Song were overly benevolent and generous; the empress said: "Being overly benevolent and generous—is it not better than being harsh and mean?"
translations.idiomatic: When someone remarked that the Song were excessively mild, the empress said: "Is excessive kindness not still better than harshness?"

sentences.zh: 一日，問女史：「黃老何教也，而竇太后好之？」

translations.literal: One day she asked a female scribe: "What teaching is Huang-Lao, that Empress Dowager Dou favored it?"
translations.idiomatic: One day she asked a female scribe: "What is the teaching of Huang-Lao, that Empress Dowager Dou favored it so?"

sentences.zh: 女史曰：「清淨無為為本。

translations.literal: The female scribe said: "Purity, stillness, and non-action as the foundation.
translations.idiomatic: The scribe answered: "Its foundation is purity, stillness, and non-action.

sentences.zh: 若絕仁棄義，民複教慈，是其教矣。」

translations.literal: If one abandons benevolence and discards righteousness, the people return to teaching kindness—that is its teaching."
translations.idiomatic: If one abandons benevolence and discards righteousness so that the people must be taught kindness again—that is its teaching."

sentences.zh: 后曰：「孝慈即仁義也，詎有絕仁義而為孝慈者哉？」

translations.literal: The empress said: "Filial piety and kindness are benevolence and righteousness; how could there be abandoning benevolence and righteousness yet practicing filial piety and kindness?"
translations.idiomatic: The empress said: "Filial piety and kindness are benevolence and righteousness themselves—how can one abandon benevolence and righteousness yet claim to be filial and kind?"

sentences.zh: 后嘗誦《小學》，求帝表章焉。

translations.literal: The empress once recited the Elementary Learning and asked the emperor to proclaim and honor it.
translations.idiomatic: She often recited the Elementary Learning and urged the emperor to give it imperial endorsement.

sentences.zh: 帝前殿決事，或震怒，后伺帝還宮，輒隨事微諫。

translations.literal: When the emperor decided affairs in the front hall and sometimes erupted in rage, the empress waited until he returned to the palace and then offered gentle remonstrance on each matter.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor grew furious over affairs in the main hall, the empress waited until he returned to the palace and gently remonstrated with him on each case.

sentences.zh: 雖帝性嚴，然為緩刑戮者數矣。

translations.literal: Although the emperor's nature was stern, yet on her account punishments and executions were relaxed many times.
translations.idiomatic: Though the emperor's nature was stern, he softened punishments and executions many times on her account.

sentences.zh: 參軍郭景祥守和州，人言其子持槊欲殺父，帝將誅之。

translations.literal: Staff officer Guo Jingxiang guarded Hezhou; people said his son held a spear intending to kill his father; the emperor was about to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: Staff officer Guo Jingxiang was defending Hezhou when reports came that his son had taken up a spear to kill him; the emperor was about to have the son executed.

sentences.zh: 后曰：「景祥止一子，人言或不實，殺之恐絕其后。」

translations.literal: The empress said: "Jingxiang has only one son; people's words may not be true; killing him may cut off his posterity."
translations.idiomatic: The empress said: "Jingxiang has only this one son; the report may be false, and to kill him would end his line."

sentences.zh: 帝廉之，果枉。

translations.literal: The emperor investigated it and indeed it was wrongful.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor investigated and found the accusation was false.

sentences.zh: 李文忠守嚴州，楊憲誣其不法，帝欲召還。

translations.literal: Li Wenzhong guarded Yanzhou; Yang Xian slandered him as unlawful; the emperor wished to summon him back.
translations.idiomatic: Li Wenzhong was defending Yanzhou when Yang Xian accused him of misconduct; the emperor intended to recall him.

sentences.zh: 后曰：「嚴，敵境也，輕易將不宜。

translations.literal: The empress said: "Yan is enemy territory; lightly changing generals is not fitting.
translations.idiomatic: The empress said: "Yanzhou lies on the enemy frontier; it is unwise to replace a commander lightly.

sentences.zh: 且文忠素賢，憲言詎可信？」

translations.literal: Moreover Wenzhong has always been worthy—how could Xian's words be trusted?"
translations.idiomatic: Besides, Wenzhong has always been capable—how can Yang Xian's words be trusted?"

sentences.zh: 帝遂已。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 文忠後卒有功。

translations.literal: Wenzhong later died after achieving merit.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhong later rendered distinguished service before his death.

sentences.zh: 學士宋濂坐孫慎罪，逮至，論死，后諫曰：「民家為子弟延師，尚以禮全終始，況天子乎？

translations.literal: Academician Song Lian was implicated in his grandson Shen's crime, arrested and brought in, sentenced to death; the empress remonstrated: "Common families who hire teachers for their sons and younger brothers still treat them with ritual from beginning to end—how much more the Son of Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: Academician Song Lian was implicated in his grandson Shen's crime, arrested, and sentenced to death. The empress remonstrated: "Even common families treat their children's teachers with courtesy from first to last—how much more should the Son of Heaven?

sentences.zh: 且濂家居，必不知情。」

translations.literal: Moreover Lian was at home; he surely did not know."
translations.idiomatic: Besides, Lian was at home and could not have known."

sentences.zh: 帝不聽。

translations.literal: The emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 會后侍帝食，不御酒肉。

translations.literal: When the empress attended the emperor at his meal, she would not partake of wine or meat.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress dined with the emperor, she abstained from wine and meat.

sentences.zh: 帝問故。

translations.literal: The emperor asked the reason.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked why.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「妾為宋先生作福事也。」

translations.literal: She replied: "Your servant is performing merit-making for Master Song."
translations.idiomatic: She replied: "I am performing merit on behalf of Master Song."

sentences.zh: 帝惻然，投箸起。

translations.literal: The emperor was moved, cast down his chopsticks and rose.
translations.idiomatic: Moved, the emperor set down his chopsticks and rose.

sentences.zh: 明日赦濂，安置茂州。

translations.literal: The next day he pardoned Lian and settled him at Maozhou.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he pardoned Lian and sent him into exile at Maozhou.

sentences.zh: 吳興富民沈秀者，助築都城三之一，又請犒軍。

translations.literal: A wealthy man of Wuxing named Shen Xiu had helped build one-third of the capital walls and again requested to reward the army.
translations.idiomatic: A wealthy man of Wuxing named Shen Xiu had funded one-third of the capital's walls and then offered to reward the army.

sentences.zh: 帝怒曰：「匹夫犒天子軍，亂民也，宜誅。」

translations.literal: The emperor angrily said: "A common fellow rewarding the Son of Heaven's army—he is a disruptive subject and ought to be executed."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor angrily said: "A commoner who rewards the Son of Heaven's army is a disturber of order and deserves death."

sentences.zh: 后諫曰：「妾聞法者，誅不法也，非以誅不祥。

translations.literal: The empress remonstrated: "Your servant has heard that law punishes what is unlawful, not what is inauspicious.
translations.idiomatic: The empress remonstrated: "I have heard that law punishes wrongdoing, not mere ill omens.

sentences.zh: 民富敵國，民自不祥。

translations.literal: When a subject's wealth rivals the state, the subject himself is inauspicious.
translations.idiomatic: When a subject's wealth rivals the state, he brings ill fortune upon himself.

sentences.zh: 不祥之民，天將災​​之​​，陛下何誅焉！」

translations.literal: An inauspicious subject—Heaven will send calamity upon him; why should Your Majesty execute him!"
translations.idiomatic: Heaven will send calamity upon such a man—why should Your Majesty execute him!"

sentences.zh: 乃釋秀，戍雲南。

translations.literal: Thereupon he released Xiu and banished him to garrison Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: He then released Xiu and banished him to Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗令重囚築城。

translations.literal: The emperor once ordered serious convicts to build the walls.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once ordered serious convicts to labor on the city walls.

sentences.zh: 后曰：「贖罪罰役，國家至恩。

translations.literal: The empress said: "Ransoming crime by penal labor is the state's utmost grace.
translations.idiomatic: The empress said: "Allowing convicts to redeem their crimes through labor is a great act of imperial grace.

sentences.zh: 但疲囚加役，恐仍不免死亡。」

translations.literal: But weary convicts with added labor—I fear they still cannot escape death."
translations.idiomatic: But worn-out prisoners forced to labor may still die."

sentences.zh: 帝乃悉赦之。

translations.literal: The emperor then pardoned them all.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then pardoned them all.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗怒責宮人，后亦佯怒，令執付宮正司議罪。

translations.literal: The emperor once angrily rebuked palace women; the empress also feigned anger and ordered them seized and handed to the Palace Rectifier's office to deliberate punishment.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor angrily rebuked palace women, the empress feigned anger too and had them handed to the Palace Rectifier to determine their punishment.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「何為？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Why do this?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked: "Why do that?"

sentences.zh: 后曰：「帝王不以喜怒加刑賞。

translations.literal: The empress said: "Emperors and kings do not add punishments and rewards according to joy and anger.
translations.idiomatic: The empress said: "A ruler must not mete out punishments and rewards according to his moods.

sentences.zh: 當陛下怒時，恐有畸重。

translations.literal: When Your Majesty is angry, I fear there may be disproportionate severity.
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty is angry, punishment may be excessive.

sentences.zh: 付宮正，則酌其平矣。

translations.literal: Handing them to the Palace Rectifier, then one weighs what is fair.
translations.idiomatic: Entrusting them to the Palace Rectifier ensures a measured judgment.

sentences.zh: 即陛下論人罪亦詔有司耳。」

translations.literal: Even when Your Majesty judges people's crimes, you also issue edicts to the responsible offices."
translations.idiomatic: Even when Your Majesty judges a crime, you issue edicts to the responsible offices."

sentences.zh: 一日，問帝：「今天下民安乎？」

translations.literal: One day she asked the emperor: "Today are the people of the realm at peace?"
translations.idiomatic: One day she asked the emperor: "Are the people of the realm at peace today?"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「此非爾所宜問也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "This is not what you ought to ask."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "That is not for you to ask."

sentences.zh: 后曰：「陛下天下父，妾辱天下母，子之安否，何可不問！」

translations.literal: The empress said: "Your Majesty is father of the realm; your servant is honored as mother of the realm—whether the children are safe or not, how can one not ask!"
translations.idiomatic: The empress said: "Your Majesty is father to the realm; I am mother to the realm—how can I not ask whether our children are safe!"

sentences.zh: 遇歲旱，輒率宮人蔬食，助祈禱；

translations.literal: When years were drought-stricken, she would lead palace women in vegetable diet to assist in prayer;
translations.idiomatic: In years of drought she led the palace women in abstaining from meat and assisted in prayers;

sentences.zh: 歲兇，則設麥飯野羹。

translations.literal: when years were famine-stricken, she would set out wheat meal and wild broth.
translations.idiomatic: in years of famine she served only wheat gruel and simple wild greens.

sentences.zh: 帝或告以振卹。

translations.literal: The emperor would sometimes tell her of relief and succor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would sometimes tell her of relief efforts.

sentences.zh: 后曰：「振卹不如蓄積之先備也。」

translations.literal: The empress said: "Relief and succor are not as good as storing up beforehand as preparation."
translations.idiomatic: The empress said: "Relief after disaster is no substitute for storing grain beforehand."

sentences.zh: 奏事官朝散，會食廷中，后命中官取飲食親嘗之。

translations.literal: When memorial-presenting officials dispersed from court, they would gather to eat in the hall; the empress ordered inner eunuchs to take food and drink and taste it personally.
translations.idiomatic: When officials who had presented memorials dined together in the hall after court, the empress had eunuchs bring their food and taste it herself.

sentences.zh: 味弗甘，遂啟帝曰：「人主自奉欲薄，養賢宜厚。」

translations.literal: When the flavor was not sweet, she then informed the emperor: "The ruler's own provisions should be thin; nourishing the worthy should be generous."
translations.idiomatic: When the food was poor, she told the emperor: "A ruler should live frugally, but nourish his worthies generously."

sentences.zh: 帝為飭光祿官。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon admonished the Director of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then reprimanded the Director of the Imperial Household.

sentences.zh: 帝幸太學還，后問生徒幾何，帝曰：「數千。」

translations.literal: When the emperor returned from visiting the Imperial Academy, the empress asked how many students there were; the emperor said: "Several thousand."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned from the Imperial Academy, the empress asked how many students there were; he said: "Several thousand."

sentences.zh: 后曰：「人才眾矣。

translations.literal: The empress said: "Talented men are numerous indeed.
translations.idiomatic: The empress said: "The realm is rich in talent indeed.

sentences.zh: 諸生有廩食，妻子將何所仰給？」

translations.literal: The students have granary provisions—upon what will their wives and children rely for support?"
translations.idiomatic: If students receive grain rations, what will their wives and children live on?"

sentences.zh: 於是立紅板倉，積糧賜其家。

translations.literal: Thereupon they established the Red Board Granary, stored grain, and granted it to their families.
translations.idiomatic: She then had the Red Board Granary established to store grain for their families.

sentences.zh: 太學生家糧自后始。

translations.literal: Imperial Academy students' family grain rations began with the empress.
translations.idiomatic: Family grain allowances for Imperial Academy students began with her.

sentences.zh: 諸將克元都，俘寶玉至。

translations.literal: When the generals took the Yuan capital, captured treasures and jades were brought in.
translations.idiomatic: When the generals captured the Yuan capital, treasures and jades were brought as booty.

sentences.zh: 后曰：「元有是而不能守，意者帝王自有寶歟。」

translations.literal: The empress said: "The Yuan had these yet could not keep them—perhaps emperors and kings have their own treasure?"
translations.idiomatic: The empress said: "The Yuan possessed these yet could not keep them—perhaps a true emperor's treasure lies elsewhere."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕知后謂得賢為寶耳。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I know the empress means that gaining the worthy is the treasure."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "I know you mean that worthy men are the true treasure."

sentences.zh: 后拜謝曰：「誠如陛下​​言。

translations.literal: The empress bowed in thanks and said: "It is truly as Your Majesty says.
translations.idiomatic: The empress bowed and said: "It is exactly as Your Majesty says.

sentences.zh: 妾與陛下起貧賤，至今日，恆恐驕縱生於奢侈，危亡起於細微，故願得賢人共理天下。」

translations.literal: Your servant and Your Majesty rose from poverty and low station to today; I constantly fear that arrogance and indulgence arise from luxury, and peril and ruin arise from trifles—therefore I wish to gain worthy men to govern the realm together."
translations.idiomatic: You and I rose from poverty to this day; I always fear that luxury breeds arrogance and that ruin begins in small things—so I pray we may govern the realm with worthy men."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「法屢更必弊，法弊則姦生；

translations.literal: She also said: When laws are changed repeatedly they must decay; when laws decay, wickedness arises;
translations.idiomatic: She also said: "When laws are changed too often they decay; when laws decay, corruption follows;

sentences.zh: 民數擾必困，民困則亂生。」

translations.literal: when the people are repeatedly disturbed they must be distressed; when the people are distressed, disorder arises."
translations.idiomatic: when the people are repeatedly harassed they grow destitute; when the people are destitute, rebellion follows."

sentences.zh: 帝歎曰：「至言也。」

translations.literal: The emperor sighed and said: "Supreme words indeed."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sighed: "Words of the highest wisdom."

sentences.zh: 命女史書之冊。

translations.literal: He ordered female scribes to write them in a book.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered female scribes to record them in a book.

sentences.zh: 其規正，類如此。

translations.literal: Her corrections and admonitions were mostly like this.
translations.idiomatic: Her remonstrances were generally of this kind.

sentences.zh: 帝每御膳，后皆躬自省視。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor took his meals, the empress personally inspected them.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor dined, the empress personally inspected his food.

sentences.zh: 平居服大練浣濯之衣，雖敝不忍易。

translations.literal: In ordinary life she wore coarse white silk garments that she washed; though worn she could not bear to replace them.
translations.idiomatic: In daily life she wore plain white silk that she washed herself, and would not discard it even when threadbare.

sentences.zh: 聞元世祖后煮故弓弦事，亦命取練織為衾裯，以賜高年煢獨。

translations.literal: Hearing of the Yuan Shizu empress boiling old bowstrings, she also ordered coarse silk woven into quilts and covers to grant to the aged and solitary.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that a Yuan empress had boiled old bowstrings for thread, she had coarse silk woven into quilts for the elderly poor.

sentences.zh: 餘帛颣絲，緝成衣裳，賜諸王妃公主，使知天桑艱難。

translations.literal: Remaining silks and knotted threads she stitched into garments and granted to the imperial princesses and princesses, to make them know heaven's mulberry's hardship.
translations.idiomatic: She stitched leftover silk into garments for imperial consorts and princesses, so they would know the hardship of sericulture.

sentences.zh: 妃嬪宮人被寵有子者，厚待之。

translations.literal: Consorts and palace women who were favored and bore sons—she treated them generously.
translations.idiomatic: She treated generously any consort or palace woman who bore the emperor a son.

sentences.zh: 命婦入朝，待之如家人禮。

translations.literal: When titled ladies entered court, she received them with family ritual.
translations.idiomatic: When noblewomen came to court, she received them as family.

sentences.zh: 帝欲訪后族人官之，后謝曰：「爵祿私外家，非法。」

translations.literal: The emperor wished to seek out the empress's clansmen and give them office; the empress declined: "Rank and salary for one's private maternal kin is not according to law."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor wished to appoint her kinsmen to office, she declined: "Bestowing rank and salary on one's own maternal kin is unlawful."

sentences.zh: 力辭而止。

translations.literal: She forcefully declined and stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: She firmly refused until he abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 然言及父母早卒，輒悲哀流涕。

translations.literal: Yet when she spoke of her parents' early death, she would grieve and shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: Yet whenever she spoke of her parents' early deaths, she wept in grief.

sentences.zh: 帝封馬公徐王，鄭媼為王夫人，修墓置廟焉。

translations.literal: The emperor enfeoffed Lord Ma as Prince of Xu, Lady Zheng as Lady of the Prince, repaired the tomb, and established a temple.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor enfeoffed Lord Ma as Prince of Xu and Lady Zheng as his consort, and built a tomb and ancestral temple for them.

sentences.zh: 洪武十五年八月寢疾。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the fifteenth year of Hongwu she fell ill in bed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Hongwu 15 she fell gravely ill.

sentences.zh: 群臣請禱祀，求良醫。

translations.literal: The ministers requested prayer sacrifices and sought good physicians.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers urged prayer sacrifices and sought skilled physicians.

sentences.zh: 后謂帝曰：「死生，命也，禱祀何益！

translations.literal: The empress told the emperor: "Life and death are fate—what use are prayer sacrifices!
translations.idiomatic: The empress told the emperor: "Life and death are ordained by fate—what good will prayers do!

sentences.zh: 且醫何能活人！

translations.literal: Moreover, how can physicians keep people alive!
translations.idiomatic: Besides, how can physicians truly save lives!

sentences.zh: 使服藥不效，得毋以妾故而罪諸醫乎？」

translations.literal: If I take medicine and it is ineffective, might not the physicians be punished on your servant's account?"
translations.idiomatic: If the medicine fails, will you not blame the physicians on my account?"

sentences.zh: 疾亟，帝問所欲言。

translations.literal: When her illness was critical, the emperor asked what she wished to say.
translations.idiomatic: As her illness worsened, the emperor asked if she had final words.

sentences.zh: 曰：「願陛下求賢納諫，慎終如始，子孫皆賢，臣民得所而已。」

translations.literal: She said: "I wish Your Majesty would seek the worthy and accept remonstrance, be cautious at the end as at the beginning, that sons and grandsons all be worthy, and ministers and people find their place—that is all."
translations.idiomatic: She said: "I pray Your Majesty will seek worthy men and heed counsel, be as careful at the end as at the beginning, that your descendants be worthy and your subjects find their place—that is all I ask."

sentences.zh: 是月丙戌崩，年五十一。

translations.literal: That month on bingxu day she died, aged fifty-one.
translations.idiomatic: She died that month on the bingxu day, at the age of fifty-one.

sentences.zh: 帝慟哭，遂不復立后。

translations.literal: The emperor wailed in grief and thereafter never again installed an empress.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned bitterly and never took another empress.

sentences.zh: 是年九月庚午葬孝陵，諡曰「孝慈皇后」。

translations.literal: That year on the gengwu day of the ninth month she was buried at Xiaoling; her posthumous title was "Empress Xiaoci."
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of that year she was buried at Xiaoling with the posthumous title "Empress Xiaoci."

sentences.zh: 宮人思之，作歌曰：「我后聖慈，化行家邦。

translations.literal: Palace women missed her and composed a song: "Our empress sage and kind, transforming conduct in home and state.
translations.idiomatic: Palace women composed a lament: "Our empress, sage and kind, transformed home and state.

sentences.zh: 撫我育我，懷德難忘。

translations.literal: She nurtured and reared us; cherishing her virtue, hard to forget.
translations.idiomatic: She nurtured and raised us; her virtue we cannot forget.

sentences.zh: 懷德難忘，於萬斯年。

translations.literal: Cherishing virtue, hard to forget—for ten thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: Her virtue we cannot forget, for ten thousand years.

sentences.zh: 毖彼下泉，悠悠蒼天。」

translations.literal: Deep are those lower springs; far and long is azure Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Deep are those lower springs; far, far is azure Heaven."

sentences.zh: 永樂元年上尊諡曰「孝慈昭憲至仁文德承天順聖高皇后」。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongle the elevated posthumous title was "Empress Xiaoci the Illustrious, Constitutive, Utmost Benevolent, Cultured and Virtuous, Receiving Heaven and Compliant with Sagacity, the High."
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 1 her elevated posthumous title became "Empress Xiaoci the Illustrious, Constitutive, Utmost Benevolent, Cultured and Virtuous, Receiving Heaven and Compliant with Sagacity, the High."

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十七年加上尊諡曰「孝慈貞化哲順仁徽成天育聖至德高皇后」。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Jiajing the added elevated posthumous title was "Empress Xiaoci the Chaste in Transformation, Wise and Compliant, Benevolent in Emblem, Completing Heaven and Nurturing Sagacity, Utmost Virtue, the High."
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 17 further honorifics were added: "Empress Xiaoci the Chaste in Transformation, Wise and Compliant, Benevolent in Emblem, Completing Heaven and Nurturing Sagacity, Utmost Virtue, the High."

sentences.zh: 成穆貴妃孫氏，陳州人。元末兵亂，妃父母俱亡，從仲兄蕃避兵揚州。青軍陷城，元帥馬世熊得之，育為義女。年十八，太祖納焉。及即位，冊封貴妃，位眾妃上。洪武七年九月薨，年三十有二。帝以妃無子，命周王橚行慈母服三年，東宮、諸王皆期。敕儒臣作《孝慈錄》。庶子為生母服三年，眾子為庶母期，自妃始。葬褚岡。賜兄瑛田租三百石，歲供禮。後附葬孝陵。淑妃李氏，壽州人。父傑，洪武初，以廣武衛指揮北征，卒於陣。十七年九月，孝慈皇后服除，冊封淑妃，攝六宮事。未幾，薨。寧妃郭氏，濠人郭山甫女。山甫善相人。太祖微時過其家，山甫相之，大驚曰：「公相貴不可言。」因謂諸子興、英曰：「吾相汝曹皆可封侯者以此。」亟遣從渡江，並遣妃侍太祖。後封寧妃。李淑妃薨，妃攝六宮事。山甫累贈營國公，興、英皆以功封侯，自有傳。

translations.literal: Noble Consort Chengmu Sun was a native of Chenzhou. In the warfare at the end of Yuan, the consort’s parents both died, and she followed her elder cousin Fan to avoid the fighting in Yangzhou. When the Qing army took the city, Marshal Ma Shixiong obtained her and raised her as an adopted daughter. At eighteen, Taizu took her into his household. After he ascended the throne, she was invested as noble consort and ranked above the other consorts. In the ninth month of Hongwu year seven she died, aged thirty-two. Because the consort had no son, the emperor ordered Zhu Su, Prince of Zhou, to observe three years’ mourning for her as a compassionate mother, while the heir apparent and all the princes observed one year. He ordered Confucian ministers to compose the Record of Filial Compassion. That secondary sons observed three years for their birth mothers and all sons observed one year for secondary mothers began with this consort. She was buried at Chugang. Her elder brother Ying was granted tax grain from fields amounting to three hundred shi, to supply the rites each year. Later she was buried adjunctively in Xiaoling. Consort Shu Li was a native of Shouzhou. Her father Jie, at the beginning of Hongwu, went north on campaign as commander of Guangwu Guard and died in battle. In the ninth month of the seventeenth year, when Empress Xiaoci’s mourning was complete, Li was invested as Consort Shu and took charge of the affairs of the six palaces. Not long after, she died. Consort Ning Guo was the daughter of Guo Shanfu of Hao. Shanfu was skilled at physiognomy. When Taizu was still lowly, he passed by his house, and Shanfu read his features. Greatly startled, he said, "Your features are noble beyond words." He then told his sons Xing and Ying, "The reason I judge that you all can be enfeoffed as marquises is this." He urgently sent them to follow Taizu across the Yangzi and also sent the consort to serve Taizu. Later she was enfeoffed as Consort Ning. After Consort Shu Li died, Consort Ning took charge of the affairs of the six palaces. Shanfu was repeatedly posthumously promoted to Duke of Yingguo, and Xing and Ying were both enfeoffed as marquises for merit; they have biographies of their own.
translations.idiomatic: Noble Consort Chengmu Sun was from Chenzhou. In the wars at the end of Yuan, both her parents died, and she followed her elder cousin Fan to take refuge in Yangzhou. When the Qing army captured the city, Marshal Ma Shixiong obtained her and raised her as an adopted daughter. At eighteen she entered Taizu’s household. After he ascended the throne, she was invested as noble consort and ranked above the other consorts. She died in the ninth month of Hongwu year seven at the age of thirty-two. Because she had no son, the emperor ordered Zhu Su, Prince of Zhou, to mourn her for three years as a compassionate mother, while the heir apparent and the other princes mourned for one year. He ordered Confucian ministers to compose the Record of Filial Compassion. The practice by which secondary sons mourned their birth mothers for three years and all sons mourned secondary mothers for one year began with her. She was buried at Chugang. Her elder brother Ying received the tax grain from three hundred shi of fields to supply the annual rites. Later she was buried with the Xiaoling. Consort Shu Li was from Shouzhou. Her father Jie, commander of Guangwu Guard at the beginning of Hongwu, campaigned north and died in battle. In the ninth month of the seventeenth year, after mourning for Empress Xiaoci was complete, Li was invested as Consort Shu and put in charge of the six palaces. She died not long after. Consort Ning Guo was the daughter of Guo Shanfu of Hao. Shanfu was skilled at physiognomy. When Taizu was still obscure, he passed by Shanfu’s house, and Shanfu read his features. Greatly startled, he said, "Your features are noble beyond words." He then told his sons Xing and Ying, "This is why I judge that all of you can be enfeoffed as marquises." He quickly sent them to follow Taizu across the Yangzi and also sent the consort to serve Taizu. Later she was made Consort Ning. After Consort Shu Li died, Consort Ning took charge of the six palaces. Shanfu was repeatedly posthumously promoted to Duke of Yingguo, and Xing and Ying were both enfeoffed as marquises for merit; they have biographies of their own.

sentences.zh: 惠帝皇后馬氏，光祿少卿全女也。

translations.literal: Huidi Empress Ma was the daughter of Vice Director of the Imperial Household Quan.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Ma of the Jianwen Emperor was the daughter of Vice Director of the Imperial Household Quan.

sentences.zh: 洪武二十八年冊為皇太孫妃。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year of Hongwu she was enfeoffed as consort of the imperial great-grandson.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 28 she was installed as consort to the heir apparent's son.

sentences.zh: 建文元年二月冊為皇后。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Jianwen she was enfeoffed as empress.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Jianwen 1 she was installed as empress.

sentences.zh: 四年六月，城陷，崩於火。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fourth year the city fell; she perished in the fire.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the fourth year, when the city fell, she perished in the flames.

sentences.zh: 成祖仁孝皇后徐氏，中山王達長女也。

translations.literal: Chengzu Empress Renxiao the Filial, née Xu, was the eldest daughter of Prince of Zhongshan Da.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Renxiao the Filial and Benevolent of Chengzu, née Xu, was the eldest daughter of Prince of Zhongshan Xu Da.

sentences.zh: 幼貞靜，好讀書，稱女諸生。

translations.literal: From youth she was chaste and quiet, loved reading books, and was called a female student.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood she was quiet and studious, devoted to books, and known as a female scholar.

sentences.zh: 太祖聞后賢淑，召達謂曰：「朕與卿，布衣交也。

translations.literal: Taizu heard the empress was worthy and virtuous, summoned Da and said: "I and you are friends from common cloth.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu heard of her worth, he summoned Da and said: "You and I were friends in humble days.

sentences.zh: 古君臣相契者，率為婚姻。

translations.literal: Ancient rulers and ministers who were in accord mostly became affines by marriage.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, rulers and ministers who were close often sealed their bond with marriage.

sentences.zh: 卿有令女，其以朕子棣配焉。」

translations.literal: You have an excellent daughter; let my son Di be matched with her."
translations.idiomatic: You have an excellent daughter; let my son Di marry her."

sentences.zh: 達頓首謝。

translations.literal: Da bowed his head in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Da kowtowed in gratitude.

sentences.zh: 洪武九年，冊為燕王妃。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Hongwu she was enfeoffed as consort of the Prince of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 9 she was installed as consort to the Prince of Yan.

sentences.zh: 高皇后深愛之。

translations.literal: The High Empress deeply loved her.
translations.idiomatic: The High Empress cherished her deeply.

sentences.zh: 從王之籓，居孝慈高皇后喪三年，蔬食如禮。

translations.literal: Following the prince to his fief, she dwelt in mourning for Empress Xiaoci the High for three years, eating vegetables according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: When she followed the prince to his fief, she observed three years of mourning for Empress Xiaoci on a vegetarian diet, as ritual required.

sentences.zh: 高皇后遺言可誦者，后一一舉之不遺。

translations.literal: The High Empress's testamentary words that could be recited—the empress recited each one without omission.
translations.idiomatic: She could recite every memorable testamentary word of the High Empress without omission.

sentences.zh: 靖難兵起，王襲大寧，李景隆乘間進圍北平。

translations.literal: When the Jingnan campaign arose, the prince raided Daning; Li Jinglong seized the interval to advance and besiege Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jingnan campaign began, the prince struck Daning while Li Jinglong seized the chance to besiege Beiping.

sentences.zh: 時仁宗以世子居守，凡部分備禦，多禀命於后。

translations.literal: At that time Renzong as heir apparent remained to guard; all deployment and defensive preparations mostly received orders from the empress.
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent Renzong held the city; most defensive dispositions were ordered by the empress.

sentences.zh: 景隆攻城急，城中兵少，后激勸將校士民妻，皆授甲登陴拒守，城卒以全。

translations.literal: Jinglong pressed the siege urgently; troops in the city were few; the empress stirred and encouraged generals', officers', and commoners' wives—all were given armor, mounted the ramparts to resist and defend, and the city in the end was preserved whole.
translations.idiomatic: As Jinglong pressed the siege with few defenders in the city, the empress roused officers' and citizens' wives to don armor and man the walls; the city was saved.

sentences.zh: 王即帝位，冊為皇后。

translations.literal: When the prince assumed the imperial throne, she was enfeoffed as empress.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince became emperor, she was installed as empress.

sentences.zh: 言：「南北每年戰鬥，兵民疲敝，宜與休息。」

translations.literal: She said: "North and south fight every year; soldiers and people are weary and exhausted—they should be given rest."
translations.idiomatic: She urged: "North and south have fought year after year until soldiers and people are exhausted; they need rest."

sentences.zh: 又言：「當世賢才皆高皇帝所遺，陛下不宜以新舊間。」

translations.literal: She also said: "The worthy talents of this age are all bequeathed by the High Emperor; Your Majesty should not distinguish old and new."
translations.idiomatic: She also said: "The worthy men of this age are all legacies of the Hongwu Emperor; Your Majesty should not distinguish old from new."

sentences.zh: 又言：「帝堯施仁自親始。」

translations.literal: She also said: "Emperor Yao practiced benevolence beginning with kin."
translations.idiomatic: She also said: "Emperor Yao practiced benevolence beginning with his own kin."

sentences.zh: 帝輒嘉納焉。

translations.literal: The emperor always praised and accepted these.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor always praised and accepted her counsel.

sentences.zh: 初，后弟增壽常以國情輸之燕，為惠帝所誅，至是欲贈爵，后力言不可。

translations.literal: Earlier the empress's younger brother Zengshou had often conveyed state intelligence to Yan and was executed by Huidi; now [the emperor] wished to grant him a noble rank; the empress forcefully said it was not permissible.
translations.idiomatic: Her brother Zengshou had secretly aided the Prince of Yan and was executed by the Jianwen Emperor; when the emperor wished to ennoble him posthumously, she firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 帝不聽，竟封定國公，命其子景昌襲，乃以告后。

translations.literal: The emperor would not listen; in the end he enfeoffed [him] as Duke of Ding, ordered his son Jingchang to inherit, and only then told the empress.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor overruled her, enfeoffed Zengshou as Duke of Ding with his son Jingchang as heir, and only then informed her.

sentences.zh: 后曰：「非妾志也。」

translations.literal: The empress said: "This was not your servant's wish."
translations.idiomatic: She said: "This was not my wish."

sentences.zh: 終弗謝。

translations.literal: In the end she never thanked [him].
translations.idiomatic: She never thanked him for it.

sentences.zh: 嘗言漢、趙二王性不順，官僚宜擇廷臣兼署之。

translations.literal: She once said the Princes of Han and Zhao were by nature disobedient; their staff should select court ministers to serve concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: She once urged that the Princes of Han and Zhao were unruly and that court ministers should be appointed to oversee their households.

sentences.zh: 一日，問：「陛下誰與圖治者？」

translations.literal: One day she asked: "With whom does Your Majesty plan governance?"
translations.idiomatic: One day she asked: "With whom does Your Majesty deliberate on governance?"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「六卿理政務，翰林職論思。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The Six Ministers manage government affairs; the Hanlin Academy's duty is deliberation and reflection."
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "The Six Ministers handle affairs; the Hanlin Academy supplies counsel."

sentences.zh: 后因請悉召見其命婦，賜冠服鈔幣。

translations.literal: The empress thereupon requested that all their titled wives be summoned to audience and granted caps, robes, and paper currency.
translations.idiomatic: She then had all their wives summoned and bestowed caps, robes, and gifts.

sentences.zh: 諭曰：「婦之事夫，奚止饋食衣服而已，必有助焉。

translations.literal: She instructed them: "A wife's service to her husband is not only presenting food and clothing—there must be assistance.
translations.idiomatic: She told them: "A wife's duty to her husband is not merely to provide food and clothing—she must also assist him.

sentences.zh: 朋友之言，有從有違，夫婦之言，婉順易入。

translations.literal: Friends' words—some are followed, some opposed; husband and wife's words are gentle and compliant, easy to enter.
translations.idiomatic: Friends may be heeded or ignored, but a wife's gentle words are easily accepted.

sentences.zh: 吾旦夕侍上，惟以生民為念，汝曹勉之。」

translations.literal: I morning and evening attend the sovereign, taking only the living people to heart—you all should strive."
translations.idiomatic: I attend the emperor day and night with the people's welfare in mind—you should do the same."

sentences.zh: 嘗採《女憲》、《女誡》作《內訓》二十篇，又類編古人嘉言善行，作《勸善書》，頒行天下。

translations.literal: She once gathered the Admonitions for Women and Cautionary Admonitions for Women to compose twenty chapters of Inner Instructions, and also classified and compiled ancient persons' fine words and good deeds to compose Exhortation to Goodness, promulgated throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: She compiled the Admonitions for Women and Cautionary Admonitions for Women into twenty chapters of Inner Instructions, and anthologized ancient moral exemplars into Exhortation to Goodness, which was circulated empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 永樂五年七月，疾革，惟勸帝愛惜百姓，廣求賢才，恩禮宗室，毋驕畜外家。又告皇太子：「曩者北平將校妻為我荷戈城守，恨未獲隨皇帝北巡，一賚卹之也。」是月乙卯崩，年四十有六。帝悲慟，為薦大齋於靈谷、天禧二寺，聽群臣致祭，光祿為具物。十月甲午，諡曰「仁孝皇后」。七年營壽陵於昌平之天壽山，又四年而陵成，以后葬焉，即長陵也。帝亦不復立后。仁宗即位，上尊諡曰「仁孝慈懿誠明莊獻配天齊聖文皇后」，祔太廟。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of Yongle year five, when her illness became critical, she only urged the emperor to cherish the people, widely seek worthy men, show favor and ritual courtesy to the imperial clan, and not let the families of consorts become arrogant. She also told the crown prince: "Formerly the wives of the generals and officers of Beiping carried spears for me and defended the city. I regret that they did not get to accompany the emperor on the northern tour; reward and aid them all." On the yimao day of that month she died, aged forty-six. The emperor grieved bitterly and held great fasts for her at Linggu and Tianxi Monasteries, allowed the assembled ministers to offer sacrifices, and had the Court of Imperial Entertainments provide the offerings. On the jiawu day of the tenth month, her posthumous title was "Empress Renxiao." In the seventh year, the Longevity Mausoleum was begun at Tianshou Mountain in Changping; four years later, when the mausoleum was completed, the empress was buried there. This was Changling. The emperor also did not establish another empress. When Renzong took the throne, he presented the elevated posthumous title "Empress Renxiao Ciyi Chengming Zhuangxian Peitian Qisheng Wen" and enshrined her in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Yongle year five, as her illness became critical, she urged the emperor only to cherish the people, seek worthy men widely, treat the imperial clan with favor and ritual courtesy, and not allow the families of consorts to grow arrogant. She also told the crown prince, "Formerly the wives of the generals and officers of Beiping carried spears for me and defended the city. I regret that they did not have the chance to accompany the emperor on his northern tour; reward and aid them all." On the yimao day of that month she died at the age of forty-six. The emperor grieved bitterly, held great fasts for her at Linggu and Tianxi Monasteries, allowed the ministers to offer sacrifices, and had the Court of Imperial Entertainments provide the offerings. On the jiawu day of the tenth month, she was given the posthumous title "Empress Renxiao." In the seventh year the Longevity Mausoleum was begun at Tianshou Mountain in Changping; four years later, when it was finished, she was buried there. This was Changling. The emperor never established another empress. When Renzong ascended, he presented her the elevated posthumous title "Empress Renxiao Ciyi Chengming Zhuangxian Peitian Qisheng Wen" and enshrined her in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 昭獻貴妃王氏，蘇州人。

translations.literal: Illustrious Presentation Noble Consort Wang was a native of Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Noble Consort Wang of Illustrious Presentation was a native of Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 永樂七年封貴妃。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Yongle she was enfeoffed as noble consort.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 7 she was ennobled as Noble Consort.

sentences.zh: 妃有賢德，事仁孝皇后恭謹，為帝所重。

translations.literal: The consort had worthy virtue, served Empress Renxiao the Filial with respect and care, and was valued by the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: She was virtuous, served Empress Renxiao with reverence, and was highly regarded by the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝晚年多急怒。

translations.literal: In his later years the emperor was often hasty and angry.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years the emperor grew irritable.

sentences.zh: 妃曲為調護，自太子諸王公主以下皆倚賴焉。

translations.literal: The consort tactfully mediated and protected; from the crown prince, princes, and princesses downward, all relied on her.
translations.idiomatic: She tactfully soothed him, and from the crown prince and princes down to the princesses, all relied on her.

sentences.zh: 十八年七月薨，禮視太祖成穆孫貴妃。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the eighteenth year she died; rites followed those for Taizu's Consort Sun of Chengmu.
translations.idiomatic: She died in the seventh month of Yongle 18; her funeral rites followed those of Consort Sun of Taizu.

sentences.zh: 恭獻賢妃權氏，朝鮮人。

translations.literal: Respectful Presentation Virtuous Consort Quan was a Korean.
translations.idiomatic: Virtuous Consort Quan of Respectful Presentation was Korean.

sentences.zh: 永樂時，朝鮮貢女充掖庭，妃與焉。

translations.literal: In Yongle times Korea presented women to fill the rear palace; the consort was among them.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongle, Korea sent tribute women to the palace; she was among them.

sentences.zh: 姿質穠農粹，善吹玉簫。

translations.literal: Her bearing and substance were lush, pure, and refined; she was skilled at playing the jade flute.
translations.idiomatic: She was beautiful and refined, and skilled at the jade flute.

sentences.zh: 帝愛憐之。

translations.literal: The emperor loved and cherished her.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor favored her deeply.

sentences.zh: 七年封賢妃，命其父永均為光祿卿。

translations.literal: In the seventh year she was enfeoffed as virtuous consort; her father Yongjun was appointed Director of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year she was made Virtuous Consort; her father Yongjun was appointed Director of the Imperial Household.

sentences.zh: 明年十月侍帝北征。

translations.literal: The next year in the tenth month she attended the emperor on the northern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: The following tenth month she accompanied the emperor on his northern campaign.

sentences.zh: 凱還，薨於臨城，葬嶧縣。

translations.literal: Returning in triumph, she died at Lincheng and was buried in Yi County.
translations.idiomatic: On the victorious return she died at Lincheng and was buried in Yi County.

sentences.zh: 仁宗誠孝皇后張氏，永城人。父麒以女貴，追封彭城伯，具《外戚傳》。洪武二十八年封燕世子妃。永樂二年封皇太子妃。仁宗立，冊為皇后。宣宗即位，尊為皇太后。英宗即位，尊為太皇太后。

translations.literal: Empress Chengxiao Zhang of Renzong was a native of Yongcheng. Her father Qi was honored because of his daughter and posthumously enfeoffed as Earl of Pengcheng; he is fully treated in the Biographies of Imperial Relatives. In Hongwu year twenty-eight she was enfeoffed as consort of the Prince of Yan’s heir. In Yongle year two she was enfeoffed as crown princess. When Renzong took the throne, she was installed as empress. When Xuanzong took the throne, she was honored as empress dowager. When Yingzong took the throne, she was honored as grand empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Chengxiao Zhang of Renzong was from Yongcheng. Her father Qi was honored because of his daughter and posthumously enfeoffed as Earl of Pengcheng; his full biography appears in Biographies of Imperial Relatives. In Hongwu 28 she was installed as consort to the heir of the Prince of Yan. In Yongle 2 she became crown princess. When Renzong ascended, she was installed as empress. When Xuanzong ascended, she was honored as empress dowager; when Yingzong ascended, as grand empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 后始為太子妃，操婦道至謹，雅得成祖及仁孝皇后歡。

translations.literal: When the empress was first crown prince's consort, she practiced the wife's way with utmost care and elegantly won Chengzu's and Empress Renxiao the Filial's favor.
translations.idiomatic: As crown princess she observed the wife's way with utmost care and won the favor of Chengzu and Empress Renxiao.

sentences.zh: 太子數為漢、趙二王所間，體肥碩不能騎射。

translations.literal: The crown prince was repeatedly set at odds by the Princes of Han and Zhao; his body was fat and large and he could not ride or shoot.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince was repeatedly slandered by the Princes of Han and Zhao; he was stout and poor at riding and archery.

sentences.zh: 成祖恚，至減太子宮膳，瀕易者屢矣，卒以后故得不廢。

translations.literal: Chengzu was angry, even reducing the crown prince's palace provisions; on the verge of replacement many times, in the end because of the empress he was not deposed.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzu was displeased, even cut the crown prince's rations, and several times nearly replaced him; only because of the empress was he not deposed.

sentences.zh: 及立為后，中外政事，莫不周知。

translations.literal: When she was established as empress, inner and outer government affairs—none she did not thoroughly know.
translations.idiomatic: Once she became empress, she was thoroughly informed of affairs within and without the court.

sentences.zh: 宣德初，軍國大議多禀聽裁決。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xuande, great deliberations on army and state mostly received her hearing for judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xuande, major military and state decisions were often referred to her for judgment.

sentences.zh: 是時海內寧泰，帝入奉起居，出奉遊宴，四方貢獻，雖微物必先上皇太后。

translations.literal: At that time within the seas there was peace and tranquility; when the emperor entered he attended her daily life, when he went out he attended her excursions and banquets; tribute from the four quarters—even trifling things—must first be presented to the empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: The realm was at peace; the emperor attended her in the morning and escorted her on outings; even the smallest tribute from the provinces was first presented to the empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 兩宮慈孝聞天下。

translations.literal: The Two Palaces' kindness and filial piety were heard throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The filial devotion between the two palaces was renowned throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 三年，太后遊西苑，皇后皇妃侍，帝親掖輿登萬歲山，奉觴上壽，獻詩頒德。

translations.literal: In the third year the empress dowager toured the Western Park; the empress and imperial consorts attended; the emperor personally supported the carriage to ascend Longevity Hill, presented a cup to offer longevity, and submitted poetry praising her virtue.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the empress dowager toured the Western Park with the empress and consorts in attendance; the emperor helped her carriage up Longevity Hill, offered a toast, and presented verses in her praise.

sentences.zh: 又明年謁長、獻二陵，帝親櫜鞬騎導。

translations.literal: The next year again she visited the Chang and Xian tombs; the emperor personally carried bow and quiver and rode as guide.
translations.idiomatic: The following year she visited the Chang and Xian tombs; the emperor himself rode ahead bearing bow and quiver.

sentences.zh: 至河橋，下馬扶輦。

translations.literal: Reaching the river bridge, he dismounted and supported the carriage.
translations.idiomatic: At the river bridge he dismounted to steady her carriage.

sentences.zh: 畿民夾道拜觀，陵旁老稚皆山呼拜迎。

translations.literal: Capital-region people lined the road to bow and observe; old and young beside the tombs all shouted from the hills in welcome.
translations.idiomatic: People of the capital lined the roads to bow; old and young near the tombs shouted their welcome from the hills.

sentences.zh: 太后顧曰：「百姓戴君，以能安之耳，皇帝宜重念。」

translations.literal: The empress dowager looked back and said: "The hundred surnames bear affection for the sovereign because he can settle them in peace—the emperor should ponder this deeply."
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager turned and said: "The people love their ruler because he keeps them at peace; the emperor should bear this deeply in mind."

sentences.zh: 及還，過農家，召老婦問生業，賜鈔幣。

translations.literal: On the return, passing a farm household, she summoned an old woman to ask about livelihood and granted paper currency.
translations.idiomatic: On the return journey she stopped at a farmhouse, questioned an old woman about her livelihood, and gave her gifts of money.

sentences.zh: 有獻蔬食酒漿者，取以賜帝，曰：「此田家味也。」

translations.literal: Someone presented vegetable food and wine; she took it to grant the emperor, saying: "This is farm-family flavor."
translations.idiomatic: When simple farm fare and wine were offered, she gave some to the emperor, saying: "This is the taste of the countryside."

sentences.zh: 從臣英國公張輔，尚書蹇義，大學士楊士奇、楊榮、金幼孜、楊溥請見行殿。

translations.literal: Following ministers—the Duke of Ying Zhang Fu, Minister Jian Yi, and Grand Secretaries Yang Shiqi, Yang Rong, Jin Youzi, and Yang Pu—requested audience at the traveling hall.
translations.idiomatic: The accompanying ministers—the Duke of Ying, Zhang Fu; Minister Jian Yi; and Grand Secretaries Yang Shiqi, Yang Rong, Jin Youzi, and Yang Pu—requested an audience at the traveling palace.

sentences.zh: 太后慰勞之，且曰：「爾等先朝舊人，勉輔嗣君。」

translations.literal: The empress dowager consoled and commended them, and said: "You are men of the previous reign; exert yourselves to assist the succeeding sovereign."
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager comforted and praised them, saying: "You are veterans of the previous reign; do your utmost to assist the new emperor."

sentences.zh: 他日，帝謂士奇曰：「皇太后謁陵還，道汝輩行事甚習。

translations.literal: Another day the emperor said to Shiqi: "When the empress dowager returned from visiting the tombs, she said you all conduct affairs very familiarly.
translations.idiomatic: Another day the emperor told Shiqi: "When the empress dowager returned from the tombs, she said you handle affairs with great familiarity.

sentences.zh: 言輔，武臣也，達大義。

translations.literal: Fu, she said, is a military minister, yet understands great principle.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fu, she said, is a military man, yet he grasps the larger principles of state.

sentences.zh: 義重厚小心，第寡斷。

translations.literal: Yi is heavy-hearted, cautious, and careful, but somewhat lacking in decision.
translations.idiomatic: Jian Yi is conscientious and cautious, but rather indecisive.

sentences.zh: 汝克正，言無避忤，先帝或數不樂，然終從汝，以不敗事。

translations.literal: You, Kezheng, speak without avoiding offense; the late emperor was sometimes displeased several times, yet in the end always followed you, so affairs were not ruined.
translations.idiomatic: You, Kezheng, speak without fear of giving offense; the late emperor was often displeased, yet in the end always heeded you, and so nothing was ruined.

sentences.zh: 又有三事，時悔不從也。」

translations.literal: There were also three matters of which she now regrets not having followed [your counsel]."
translations.idiomatic: There were also three matters she now regretted not having followed."

sentences.zh: 太后遇外家嚴，弟升至淳謹，然不許預議國事。

translations.literal: The empress dowager was strict toward her maternal kin; her younger brother Sheng was simple and careful, yet she did not permit him to participate in deliberating state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager was strict with her own kin: her younger brother Sheng was honest and prudent, yet she never allowed him to take part in state deliberations.

sentences.zh: 宣宗崩，英宗方九歲，宮中訛言將召立襄王矣。

translations.literal: When Xuande died, Yingzong was only nine; a false rumor in the palace said the Prince of Xiang would be summoned and established.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xuande Emperor died, Yingzong was only nine years old, and a rumor spread through the palace that the Prince of Xiang would be summoned and enthroned.

sentences.zh: 太后趣召諸大臣至乾清宮，指太子泣曰：「此新天子也。」

translations.literal: The empress dowager hastily summoned the great ministers to the Palace of Heavenly Purity, pointed to the crown prince, and weeping said: "This is the new Son of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager hastily summoned the chief ministers to the Palace of Heavenly Purity, pointed to the crown prince, and weeping said: "This is the new emperor."

sentences.zh: 君臣呼萬歲，浮言乃息。

translations.literal: Ministers and ruler cried "Ten thousand years!" and the floating talk then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers and sovereign cried "Long live the emperor!" and the rumors subsided.

sentences.zh: 大臣請太后垂簾聽政，太后曰：「毋壞祖宗法。

translations.literal: The ministers requested the empress dowager hold court from behind a screen; the empress dowager said: "Do not damage the ancestral institutions.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers asked the empress dowager to rule from behind a screen, but she said: "Do not violate the institutions of our ancestors.

sentences.zh: 第悉罷一切不急務。」

translations.literal: Only dismiss entirely all non-urgent affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Only cancel every nonessential undertaking."

sentences.zh: 時時勗帝向學，委任股肱，以故王振雖寵於帝，終太后世不敢專大政。

translations.literal: She frequently exhorted the emperor to devote himself to learning and entrusted the core ministers; for this reason, though Wang Zhen was favored by the emperor, through the empress dowager's lifetime he did not dare monopolize great government.
translations.idiomatic: She constantly urged the emperor to apply himself to his studies and entrusted affairs to his chief ministers; for this reason, though Wang Zhen enjoyed the emperor's favor, he did not dare seize control of government while the empress dowager lived.

sentences.zh: 正統七年十月崩。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of Zhengtong 7 she died.
translations.idiomatic: She died in the tenth month of Zhengtong 7.

sentences.zh: 當大漸，召士奇、溥入，命中官問國家尚有何大事未辦者。

translations.literal: When death was near, she summoned Shiqi and Pu and ordered eunuchs to ask what great state affairs remained unfinished.
translations.idiomatic: As she lay dying, she summoned Yang Shiqi and Yang Pu and had eunuchs ask what major state business still remained undone.

sentences.zh: 士奇舉三事。

translations.literal: Shiqi cited three matters.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi named three matters.

sentences.zh: 一謂「建庶人雖亡，當修《實錄》」；

translations.literal: One was that "though the Deprived Heir is dead, the Veritable Records should be compiled";
translations.idiomatic: The first was that "though the Deprived Heir is dead, his Veritable Records should still be compiled";

sentences.zh: 一謂「太宗詔有『收方孝孺諸臣遺書者死』，宜弛其禁」；

translations.literal: one was that "Taizong's edict stated 'whoever collects the surviving writings of Fang Xiaoru and his colleagues shall die'—the prohibition should be relaxed";
translations.idiomatic: the second was that "Taizong's edict declared 'death to whoever collects the surviving writings of Fang Xiaoru and his followers'—that ban should be lifted";

sentences.zh: 其三未及奏上，而太后已崩。

translations.literal: the third had not yet been memorialized when the empress dowager already died.
translations.idiomatic: the third had not yet been submitted when the empress dowager died.

sentences.zh: 遺詔勉大臣佐帝惇行仁政，語甚諄篤。

translations.literal: Her testamentary edict exhorted the ministers to assist the emperor in earnestly practicing benevolent governance; the words were very earnest.
translations.idiomatic: Her deathbed edict urged the ministers to help the emperor govern with sincere benevolence; its language was deeply earnest.

sentences.zh: 上尊諡曰「誠孝恭肅明德弘仁順天啟聖昭皇后」，合葬獻陵，祔太廟。

translations.literal: Posthumous honors were conferred as "Empress Zhao of Sincere Filiality, Reverent Solemnity, Bright Virtue, Expansive Benevolence, and Heaven-Accorded Sage Enlightenment"; she was buried jointly at the Xian tomb and enshrined in the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: She was posthumously titled "Empress Zhao of Sincere Filiality, Reverent Solemnity, Bright Virtue, Expansive Benevolence, and Heaven-Accorded Sage Enlightenment"; she was buried with the Xuande Emperor at the Xian Mausoleum and enshrined in the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 宣宗恭讓皇后胡氏，名善祥，濟寧人。

translations.literal: Xuande's Deposed Empress Hu, named Shansxiang, was a native of Jining.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Hu of Deposed Submission, consort of the Xuande Emperor, was named Shansxiang and came from Jining.

sentences.zh: 永樂十五年選為皇太孫妃。

translations.literal: In Yongle 15 she was selected as consort to the imperial grandson.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 15 she was chosen as consort to the imperial grandson.

sentences.zh: 已，為皇太子妃。

translations.literal: Thereafter she became consort to the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Later she became crown princess.

sentences.zh: 宣宗即位，立為皇后。

translations.literal: When Xuande acceded, she was established as empress.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuande took the throne, she was installed as empress.

sentences.zh: 時孫貴妃有寵，后未有子，又善病。

translations.literal: At that time Noble Consort Sun was favored; the empress had no son and was often ill.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Noble Consort Sun was in favor; the empress had borne no son and was frequently ill.

sentences.zh: 三年春，帝令后上表辭位，乃退居長安宮，賜號靜慈仙師，而冊貴妃為后。

translations.literal: In spring of the third year the emperor ordered the empress to submit a memorial resigning her position; she thereupon withdrew to Chang'an Palace, was granted the title Tranquil Kindness Immortal Master, and the noble consort was enfeoffed as empress.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the third year the emperor had the empress submit a memorial abdicating; she withdrew to Chang'an Palace, was given the title Tranquil Kindness Immortal Master, and the noble consort was installed as empress.

sentences.zh: 諸大臣張輔、蹇義、夏原吉、楊士奇、楊榮等不能爭。

translations.literal: The great ministers Zhang Fu, Jian Yi, Xia Yuanji, Yang Shiqi, Yang Rong, and others could not protest.
translations.idiomatic: Leading ministers such as Zhang Fu, Jian Yi, Xia Yuanji, Yang Shiqi, and Yang Rong were unable to object.

sentences.zh: 張太后憫后賢，常召居清寧宮。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Zhang pitied the empress's worth; she often summoned her to dwell in Qingning Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Zhang, pitying the deposed empress's virtue, often summoned her to stay in Qingning Palace.

sentences.zh: 內廷朝宴，命居孫后上。

translations.literal: At inner-court morning banquets she ordered her to sit above Empress Sun.
translations.idiomatic: At palace banquets she ordered Hu to be seated above Empress Sun.

sentences.zh: 孫后常怏怏。

translations.literal: Empress Sun was often displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Sun was often resentful.

sentences.zh: 正統七年十月，太皇太后崩，后痛哭不已，逾年亦崩，用嬪御禮葬金山。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of Zhengtong 7 the grand empress dowager died; the empress wept without cease, and more than a year later she too died, buried at Jinshan with the rites of a consort or attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Zhengtong 7 the grand empress dowager died; the deposed empress wept without end, and a little over a year later she too died and was buried at Jinshan with the rites due a concubine.

sentences.zh: 后無過被廢，天下聞而憐之。

translations.literal: The empress was deposed though without fault; when the realm heard of it, all pitied her.
translations.idiomatic: She had been deposed without fault, and all who heard of it pitied her.

sentences.zh: 宣宗後亦悔。

translations.literal: Afterwards Xuande also came to regret it.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Xuande Emperor also came to regret it.

sentences.zh: 嘗自解曰：「此朕少年事。」

translations.literal: He once explained himself, saying: "This was a matter of my youth."
translations.idiomatic: He once excused himself, saying: "That was the act of my youth."

sentences.zh: 天順六年，孫太后崩，錢皇后為英宗言：「后賢而無罪，廢為仙師。
