translations.literal: In Tianshun 6, when Empress Dowager Sun died, Empress Qian spoke to Yingzong: "The empress was worthy and without guilt, yet was deposed and made an Immortal Master.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianshun 6, after Empress Dowager Sun died, Empress Qian told Yingzong: "The empress was virtuous and innocent, yet was deposed and made an Immortal Master.

sentences.zh: 其沒也，人畏太后，殮葬皆不如禮。」

translations.literal: At her death people feared the empress dowager; encoffining and burial were all unlike proper ritual."
translations.idiomatic: When she died, people feared the empress dowager, and her encoffining and burial fell far short of proper rites."

sentences.zh: 因勸復其位號。

translations.literal: She thereupon urged restoration of her rank and title.
translations.idiomatic: She therefore urged that her rank and title be restored.

sentences.zh: 英宗問大學士李賢。

translations.literal: Yingzong asked Grand Secretary Li Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzong consulted Grand Secretary Li Xian.

sentences.zh: 賢對曰：「陛下此心，天地鬼神實臨之。

translations.literal: Xian replied: "Your Majesty's heart in this—Heaven, Earth, and the spirits truly witness it.
translations.idiomatic: Xian answered: "Your Majesty's intent in this is witnessed by Heaven, Earth, and the spirits.

sentences.zh: 然臣以陵寢、享殿、神主俱宜如奉先殿式，庶稱陛下明孝。」

translations.literal: Yet your servant holds that tomb chambers, spirit halls, and spirit tablets should all follow the model of the Hall of Ancestral Reverence, so that Your Majesty's enlightened filial piety may be fitly expressed."
translations.idiomatic: Yet I believe her tomb, spirit hall, and tablet should all follow the model of the Hall of Ancestral Reverence, so that Your Majesty's enlightened filial piety may be fully shown."

sentences.zh: 七年閏七月，上尊諡曰「恭讓誠順康穆靜慈章皇后」，修陵寢，不祔廟。

translations.literal: In the intercalary seventh month of the seventh year posthumous honors were conferred as "Empress Zhang of Deposed Submission, Sincere Compliance, Secure Serenity, and Tranquil Kindness"; tomb chambers were built, but she was not enshrined in the temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary seventh month of Tianshun 7 she was posthumously titled "Empress Zhang of Deposed Submission, Sincere Compliance, Secure Serenity, and Tranquil Kindness"; a mausoleum was built for her, but she was not enshrined in the temple.

sentences.zh: 宣宗孝恭皇后孫氏，鄒平人。

translations.literal: Xuande's Empress Sun of Filial Reverence, surnamed Sun, was a native of Zouping.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Sun of Filial Reverence, consort of the Xuande Emperor, came from Zouping.

sentences.zh: 幼有美色。

translations.literal: In youth she had great beauty.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a girl she was strikingly beautiful.

sentences.zh: 父忠，永城縣主簿也。

translations.literal: Her father Zhong was a registrar of Yongcheng County.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Zhong was a registrar in Yongcheng County.

sentences.zh: 誠孝皇后母彭城伯夫人，故永城人，時時入禁中，言忠有賢女，遂得入宮。

translations.literal: The mother of Empress Xiaocheng was the Lady of Pengcheng, a native of Yongcheng; she often entered the forbidden palace and spoke of Zhong's worthy daughter, and so [Sun] gained entry to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xiaocheng's mother, the Lady of Pengcheng, was also from Yongcheng; she often entered the palace and praised Zhong's worthy daughter, and so Sun was brought into court.

sentences.zh: 方十餘歲，成祖命誠孝后育之。

translations.literal: When she was just over ten, Chengzu ordered Empress Xiaocheng to raise her.
translations.idiomatic: When she was barely in her teens, the Yongle Emperor had Empress Xiaocheng raise her.

sentences.zh: 已而宣宗婚，詔選濟寧胡氏為妃，而以孫氏為嬪。

translations.literal: Thereafter when Xuande wed, an edict selected Hu of Jining as consort and made Sun a concubine.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuande married, an edict chose Hu of Jining as his principal consort and made Sun a concubine.

sentences.zh: 宣宗即位，封貴妃。

translations.literal: When Xuande acceded, she was enfeoffed as noble consort.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuande took the throne, she was made Noble Consort.

sentences.zh: 故事：皇后金寶金冊，貴妃以下，有冊無寶。

translations.literal: By precedent: the empress received a golden seal and golden patent; noble consorts and below received the patent but not the seal.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent the empress received both a golden seal and a golden patent, while noble consorts and below received the patent alone.

sentences.zh: 妃有寵，宣德元年五月，帝請於太后，制金寶賜焉。

translations.literal: The consort was favored; in the fifth month of Xuande 1 the emperor requested of the empress dowager and had a golden seal made and granted to her.
translations.idiomatic: Because the consort was favored, in the fifth month of Xuande 1 the emperor asked the empress dowager's permission and had a golden seal made and bestowed on her.

sentences.zh: 貴妃有寶自此始。

translations.literal: From this noble consorts receiving seals began.
translations.idiomatic: From this time noble consorts began to receive golden seals.

sentences.zh: 妃亦無子，陰取宮人子為己子，即英宗也，由是眷寵益重。

translations.literal: The consort likewise had no son; secretly she took a palace woman's child as her own—this was Yingzong—and by this her favor grew ever heavier.
translations.idiomatic: The consort too had no son; she secretly took a palace woman's child as her own—this was Yingzong—and her favor therefore grew all the greater.

sentences.zh: 胡后上表遜位，請早定國本。

translations.literal: Empress Hu submitted a memorial yielding her position, requesting early fixation of the foundation of state.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Hu submitted a memorial abdicating and asked that the succession be settled promptly.

sentences.zh: 妃偽辭曰：「后病痊自有子，吾子敢先后子耶？」

translations.literal: The consort falsely declined, saying: "When the empress's illness heals she will have her own son; how would my son dare to precede the empress's son?"
translations.idiomatic: The consort feigned refusal, saying: "When the empress recovers she will bear a son of her own; how could my son dare take precedence over the empress's son?"

sentences.zh: 三年三月，胡后廢，遂冊為皇后。

translations.literal: In the third month of the third year Empress Hu was deposed and [Sun] was thereupon enfeoffed as empress.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the third year Empress Hu was deposed, and Sun was installed as empress.

sentences.zh: 英宗立，尊為皇太后。

translations.literal: When Yingzong was enthroned, [Sun] was honored as empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: When Yingzong ascended the throne, she was honored as empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 英宗北狩，太后命郕王監國。景帝即位，尊為上聖皇太后。時英宗在迤北，數寄禦寒衣裘。及還，幽南宮，太后數入省視。石亨等謀奪門，先密白太后。許之。英宗復辟，上徽號曰「聖烈慈壽皇太后」。明興，宮闈徽號亦自此始。天順六年九月崩，上尊諡曰「孝恭懿憲慈仁莊烈齊天配聖章皇后」，合葬景陵，祔太廟。而英宗生母，人卒無知之者。

translations.literal: When Yingzong was taken north, the empress dowager ordered the Prince of Cheng to supervise the state. When the Jingtai Emperor took the throne, she was honored as Supreme Sagely Empress Dowager. At that time Yingzong was north of the frontier, and she repeatedly sent him winter clothes and furs. When he returned and was confined in the Southern Palace, the empress dowager often entered to visit and look after him. When Shi Heng and the others plotted the Seizing of the Gate, they first secretly reported it to the empress dowager. She approved it. After Yingzong was restored to the throne, he presented the honorific title "Sagely, Heroic, Compassionate, and Long-Lived Empress Dowager." In the Ming, honorific titles for the inner palace began from this. In the ninth month of Tianshun year six she died, and the emperor presented the posthumous title "Empress Xiaogong Yixian Ciren Zhuanglie Qitian Peisheng Zhang." She was buried together in Jingling and enshrined in the Imperial Ancestral Temple. As for Yingzong’s birth mother, people in the end never knew who she was.
translations.idiomatic: When Yingzong was taken north, the empress dowager ordered the Prince of Cheng to supervise the realm. When the Jingtai Emperor ascended, she was honored as Supreme Sagely Empress Dowager. While Yingzong was north of the frontier, she repeatedly sent him winter clothing and furs. After he returned and was confined in the Southern Palace, she often went in to visit him. When Shi Heng and the others plotted the Seizing of the Gate, they first reported it secretly to the empress dowager, and she approved. Once Yingzong was restored, he gave her the honorific title "Sagely, Heroic, Compassionate, and Long-Lived Empress Dowager." In the Ming, palace honorific titles began from this. She died in the ninth month of Tianshun year six, and the emperor gave her the posthumous title "Empress Xiaogong Yixian Ciren Zhuanglie Qitian Peisheng Zhang." She was buried with him in Jingling and enshrined in the Imperial Ancestral Temple. As for Yingzong’s birth mother, no one ever knew who she was.

sentences.zh: 吳太后，景帝母也，丹徒人。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Wu, mother of Jingdi, was a native of Dantu.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Wu, mother of the Jingtai Emperor, was from Dantu.

sentences.zh: 宣宗為太子時，選入宮。

translations.literal: When Xuande was crown prince, she was selected and entered the palace.
translations.idiomatic: She was chosen for the palace when Xuande was still crown prince.

sentences.zh: 宣德三年封賢妃。

translations.literal: In Xuande 3 she was enfeoffed as Virtuous Consort.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuande 3 she was made Virtuous Consort.

sentences.zh: 景帝即位，尊為皇太后。

translations.literal: When Jingdi acceded, she was honored as empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingtai took the throne, she was honored as empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 英宗復辟，復稱宣廟賢妃。

translations.literal: When Yingzong restored his rule, she was again styled Virtuous Consort of the Xuande Temple.
translations.idiomatic: After Yingzong's restoration she was again styled Virtuous Consort of the Xuande Temple.

sentences.zh: 成化中薨。

translations.literal: In the Chenghua reign she died.
translations.idiomatic: She died during the Chenghua reign.

sentences.zh: 郭嬪，名愛，字善理，鳳陽人。賢而有文，入宮二旬而卒。自知死期，書楚聲以自哀。詞曰：「修短有數兮，不足較也。生而如夢兮，死則覺也。先吾親而歸兮，慚予之失孝也。心悽悽而不能已兮，是則可悼也。」正統元年八月，追贈皇庶母惠妃何氏為貴妃，諡「端靜」；趙氏為賢妃，諡「純靜」；吳氏為惠妃，諡「貞順」；焦氏為淑妃，諡「莊靜」；曹氏為敬妃，諡「莊順」；徐氏為順妃，諡「貞惠」；袁氏為麗妃，諡「恭定」；諸氏為淑妃，諡「貞靜」；李氏為充妃，諡「恭順」；何氏為成妃，諡「肅僖」。冊文曰：「茲委身而蹈義，隨龍馭以上賓，宜薦徽稱，用彰節行。」蓋宣宗殉葬宮妃也。初，太祖崩，宮人多從死者。建文、永樂時，相繼優恤。若張鳳、李衡、趙福、張璧、汪賓諸家，皆自錦衣衛所試百戶、散騎帶刀舍人進千百戶，帶俸世襲，人謂之「太祖朝天女戶」。歷成祖，仁、宣二宗亦皆用殉。景帝以郕王薨，猶用其制，蓋當時王府皆然。至英宗遺詔，始罷之。

translations.literal: Concubine Guo, named Ai and styled Shanli, was a native of Fengyang. She was worthy and had literary talent, but died twenty days after entering the palace. Knowing the time of her death herself, she wrote a lament in Chu style to mourn herself. Its words said: "Length and shortness have their allotted number, and are not worth comparing. Life is like a dream, and death is awakening. To return before my parents shames me for failing in filial devotion. My heart grieves and cannot stop; this is what may be mourned." In the eighth month of Zhengtong year one, the emperor posthumously promoted his imperial secondary mothers: Consort Hui He was made noble consort, with the posthumous title "Upright and Tranquil"; Zhao was made Consort Xian, with the posthumous title "Pure and Tranquil"; Wu was made Consort Hui, with the posthumous title "Chaste and Obedient"; Jiao was made Consort Shu, with the posthumous title "Dignified and Tranquil"; Cao was made Consort Jing, with the posthumous title "Dignified and Obedient"; Xu was made Consort Shun, with the posthumous title "Chaste and Kind"; Yuan was made Consort Li, with the posthumous title "Reverent and Settled"; Zhu was made Consort Shu, with the posthumous title "Chaste and Tranquil"; Li was made Consort Chong, with the posthumous title "Reverent and Obedient"; He was made Consort Cheng, with the posthumous title "Solemn and Harmonious." The investiture text said, "Now they entrusted their bodies and trod righteousness, following the dragon chariot to become honored guests above; it is fitting to offer them splendid titles, thereby manifesting their chastity and conduct." These were evidently the palace consorts buried in sacrifice with Xuanzong. At first, when Taizu died, many palace women followed him in death. In the Jianwen and Yongle reigns, their families were successively given favor and aid. Families such as those of Zhang Feng, Li Heng, Zhao Fu, Zhang Bi, and Wang Bin were all advanced from probationary hundred-household officers of the Embroidered-Uniform Guard, mounted guardsmen, or sword-bearing attendants to hundred-household or thousand-household offices, with salaried hereditary status. People called them "households of the women who attended Taizu to Heaven." Through Chengzu and the Renzong and Xuanzong reigns, sacrifice in death was still used. When the Jingtai Emperor died as Prince of Cheng, the same system was still used; this was evidently the case for all princely households at the time. Only with Yingzong’s testamentary edict was it finally abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Concubine Guo, named Ai and styled Shanli, was from Fengyang. She was worthy and literary, but died twenty days after entering the palace. Knowing the time of her death, she wrote a Chu-style lament for herself: "Length and shortness have their allotted number; they are not worth comparing. Life is like a dream; death is awakening. To return before my parents shames me for failing in filial devotion. My heart grieves and cannot stop; this is what may be mourned." In the eighth month of Zhengtong year one, the emperor posthumously promoted his imperial secondary mothers: Consort Hui He became noble consort with the posthumous title "Upright and Tranquil"; Zhao became Consort Xian, "Pure and Tranquil"; Wu became Consort Hui, "Chaste and Obedient"; Jiao became Consort Shu, "Dignified and Tranquil"; Cao became Consort Jing, "Dignified and Obedient"; Xu became Consort Shun, "Chaste and Kind"; Yuan became Consort Li, "Reverent and Settled"; Zhu became Consort Shu, "Chaste and Tranquil"; Li became Consort Chong, "Reverent and Obedient"; and He became Consort Cheng, "Solemn and Harmonious." The investiture text said, "They entrusted their bodies and trod righteousness, following the dragon chariot to become honored guests above; splendid titles should be offered to display their chastity and conduct." These were evidently the palace consorts buried in sacrifice with Xuanzong. At first, when Taizu died, many palace women followed him in death. During Jianwen and Yongle, their families were successively favored and supported. Families such as Zhang Feng, Li Heng, Zhao Fu, Zhang Bi, and Wang Bin all rose from probationary hundred-household officers of the Embroidered-Uniform Guard, mounted guardsmen, or sword-bearing attendants to hundred-household or thousand-household offices, with salaried hereditary status. People called them "households of the women who attended Taizu to Heaven." Under Chengzu, Renzong, and Xuanzong, burial sacrifice was still used. When the Jingtai Emperor died as Prince of Cheng, the same system was still used; evidently this was true of all princely households then. It was only abolished by Yingzong’s testamentary edict.

sentences.zh: 英宗孝莊皇后錢氏，海州人。

translations.literal: Yingzong's Empress Qian of Filial Serenity, surnamed Qian, was a native of Haizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Qian of Filial Serenity, consort of the Yingzong Emperor, came from Haizhou.

sentences.zh: 正統七年立為后。

translations.literal: In Zhengtong 7 she was established as empress.
translations.idiomatic: She was installed as empress in Zhengtong 7.

sentences.zh: 帝憫后族單微，欲侯之，后輒遜謝。

translations.literal: The emperor pitied that the empress's clan was few and humble and wished to ennoble them; the empress always modestly declined.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, pitying her family's modest station, wished to ennoble her kin, but the empress always modestly refused.

sentences.zh: 故后家獨無封。

translations.literal: Therefore the empress's family alone received no enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Thus hers was the only empress's family left without a noble title.

sentences.zh: 英宗北狩，傾中宮貲佐迎駕。

translations.literal: When Yingzong went north on campaign and was captured, she exhausted the empress's treasury to aid in welcoming the emperor home.
translations.idiomatic: When Yingzong was taken captive on the northern campaign, she spent the empress's entire treasury to help ransom and welcome him home.

sentences.zh: 夜哀泣籲天，倦即臥地，損一股。

translations.literal: At night she wept in grief and called to Heaven; when weary she would lie on the ground, injuring a leg.
translations.idiomatic: Night after night she wept and prayed to Heaven; when exhaustion overcame her she would lie on the bare ground and injured one leg.

sentences.zh: 以哭泣复損一目。

translations.literal: From weeping she also lost sight in one eye.
translations.idiomatic: From weeping she also lost the sight of one eye.

sentences.zh: 英宗在南宮，不自得，后曲為慰解。

translations.literal: When Yingzong was in the Southern Palace, ill at ease, the empress tactfully consoled and relieved him.
translations.idiomatic: While Yingzong languished in the Southern Palace, the empress gently comforted and reassured him.

sentences.zh: 后無子，周貴妃有子，立為皇太子。

translations.literal: The empress had no son; Noble Consort Zhou had a son who was established as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: The empress bore no son; Noble Consort Zhou's son was made crown prince.

sentences.zh: 英宗大漸，遺命曰：「錢皇后千秋萬歲后，與朕同葬。」

translations.literal: When Yingzong was near death, his testamentary command stated: "After Empress Qian's thousand autumns and ten thousand years, bury her together with me."
translations.idiomatic: As Yingzong lay dying, he commanded: "When Empress Qian passes away, bury her with me."

sentences.zh: 大學士李賢退而書之冊。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Li Xian withdrew and wrote it in the record.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Li Xian withdrew and recorded the command in writing.

sentences.zh: 憲宗立，上兩宮徽號，下廷臣議。

translations.literal: When Xianzong was enthroned, he proposed honorific titles for the Two Palaces and submitted them to court ministers for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzong took the throne, he proposed honorific titles for the two palaces and referred the matter to the court.

sentences.zh: 太監夏時希貴妃意，傳諭獨尊貴妃為皇太后。

translations.literal: The eunuch Xia Shi, seeking to please the noble consort, transmitted an edict honoring the noble consort alone as empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Xia Shi, currying favor with Noble Consort Zhou, conveyed an edict honoring her alone as empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 大學士李賢、彭時力爭，乃兩宮並尊，而稱后為慈懿​​皇太后。

translations.literal: Grand Secretaries Li Xian and Peng Shi forcefully protested; thereupon both palaces were honored equally, and the empress was styled Empress Dowager of Kind Benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretaries Li Xian and Peng Shi protested vigorously; both palaces were then honored equally, and the empress was styled Empress Dowager of Kind Benevolence.

sentences.zh: 及營裕陵，賢、時請營三壙，下廷議。

translations.literal: When the Yu tomb was being built, Xian and Shi requested construction of three burial chambers and submitted it to court deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: When work began on the Yu Mausoleum, Li Xian and Peng Shi asked that three burial chambers be built and submitted the proposal for court debate.

sentences.zh: 夏時復言不可，事竟寢。

translations.literal: Xia Shi again said it was not permissible; the matter in the end was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Shi again objected, and the proposal was finally dropped.

sentences.zh: 成化四年六月，太后崩，周太后不欲后合葬。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of Chenghua 4 the empress dowager died; Empress Dowager Zhou did not wish the empress buried jointly.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Chenghua 4 Empress Dowager Qian died; Empress Dowager Zhou did not want her buried with the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝使夏時、懷恩召大臣議。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Xia Shi and Huai'en to summon the ministers to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Xia Shi and Huai'en to summon the ministers for consultation.

sentences.zh: 彭時首對曰：「合葬裕陵，主祔廟，定禮也。」

translations.literal: Peng Shi answered first: "Joint burial at the Yu tomb with her spirit tablet enshrined in the temple is settled ritual."
translations.idiomatic: Peng Shi answered first: "Joint burial at the Yu Mausoleum with her tablet enshrined in the temple is established ritual."

sentences.zh: 翼日，帝召問，時對如前。

translations.literal: The next day the emperor summoned and questioned him; Shi answered as before.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the emperor summoned him again; Peng Shi gave the same answer.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕豈不知，慮他日妨母后耳。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Do I not know this? I fear it would one day obstruct the empress dowager."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Do I not know that? I only fear it would one day slight my mother the empress dowager."

sentences.zh: 時曰：「皇上孝事兩宮，聖德彰聞。

translations.literal: Shi said: "Your Majesty filially serves the Two Palaces; sagely virtue is brilliantly known.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Shi said: "Your Majesty serves both palaces with filial devotion; your virtue is renowned.

sentences.zh: 禮之所合，孝之所歸也。」

translations.literal: What ritual accords with is where filial piety resides."
translations.idiomatic: What ritual requires is where true filial piety lies."

sentences.zh: 商輅亦言：「不祔葬，損聖德。」

translations.literal: Shang Lu also said: "Not enshrining and burying jointly damages sagely virtue."
translations.idiomatic: Shang Lu also said: "To refuse joint burial and enshrinement would tarnish your virtue."

sentences.zh: 劉定之曰：「孝從義，不從命。」

translations.literal: Liu Dingzhi said: "Filial piety follows righteousness, not commands."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Dingzhi said: "Filial piety follows what is right, not mere obedience."

sentences.zh: 帝默然久之，曰：「不從命尚得為孝耶！」

translations.literal: The emperor was silent a long while and said: "If one does not follow a command, can that still be filial piety?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was silent for a long time, then said: "If I disobey her, how can that be filial?"

sentences.zh: 時力請合葬裕陵左，而虛右以待周太后。

translations.literal: Shi forcefully requested joint burial at the left of the Yu tomb, leaving the right vacant to await Empress Dowager Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Shi urgently pleaded that she be buried on the left side of the Yu Mausoleum, leaving the right side vacant for Empress Dowager Zhou.

sentences.zh: 已，復與大臣疏爭，帝再下廷議。

translations.literal: Thereupon he again memorialized disputing with the ministers; the emperor once more submitted it to court deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: He then memorialized again with the other ministers; the emperor once more referred the matter to court debate.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書李秉、禮部尚書姚夔集廷臣九十九人議，皆請如時言。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Li Bing and Minister of Rites Yao Kui gathered ninety-nine court ministers in deliberation; all requested as Shi had said.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bing, Minister of Personnel, and Yao Kui, Minister of Rites, convened ninety-nine officials; all supported Peng Shi's view.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿等言是，顧朕屢請太后未得命。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Your words are correct, but I have repeatedly requested permission of the empress dowager and have not received it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "You are right, but I have repeatedly asked the empress dowager and she has not consented.

sentences.zh: 乖禮非孝，違親亦非孝。」

translations.literal: To violate ritual is not filial; to disobey a parent is also not filial."
translations.idiomatic: To violate ritual is unfilial, but to defy a parent is unfilial too."

sentences.zh: 明日，詹事柯潛、給事中魏元等上疏，又明日，夔等合疏上，皆執議如初。

translations.literal: The next day Junior Guardian Ke Qian, Investigating Censor Wei Yuan, and others submitted memorials; again the next day Yao Kui and others jointly submitted a memorial—all held to their original opinion.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Ke Qian, Wei Yuan, and others submitted memorials; the day after, Yao Kui and others submitted a joint memorial—all insisting on the same position.

sentences.zh: 中旨猶諭別擇葬地。

translations.literal: An imperial command from within still directed selection of a separate burial site.
translations.idiomatic: An edict from the palace still ordered a separate burial site to be chosen.

sentences.zh: 於是百官伏哭文華門外。

translations.literal: Thereupon the hundred officers prostrated themselves weeping outside the Gate of Literary Splendor.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the officials prostrated themselves and wept outside the Gate of Literary Splendor.

sentences.zh: 帝命群臣退。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the assembled ministers to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the ministers to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 眾叩頭，不得旨不敢退。

translations.literal: They kowtowed; without receiving permission they did not dare withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: They kowtowed and, without receiving leave, dared not rise.

sentences.zh: 自已至申，乃得允。

translations.literal: From the si hour to the shen hour, only then did they receive permission.
translations.idiomatic: From mid-morning until late afternoon, they received permission to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 眾呼萬歲出。

translations.literal: The assembly shouted "Ten thousand years!" and departed.
translations.idiomatic: They shouted "Long live the emperor!" and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 事詳時、夔傳中。

translations.literal: The affair is detailed in the biographies of Shi and Kui.
translations.idiomatic: The full account appears in the biographies of Peng Shi and Yao Kui.

sentences.zh: 是年七月上尊諡曰「孝莊獻穆弘惠顯仁恭天欽聖睿皇后」，祔太廟。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of that year a posthumous honorific title was conferred: "Empress Xiaozhuang Xianmu Honghui Xianren Gongtian Qinsheng Rui," and she was enshrined in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of that year she was given the posthumous title "Empress Xiaozhuang Xianmu Honghui Xianren Gongtian Qinsheng Rui" and enshrined in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 九月合葬裕陵，異隧，距英宗玄堂數丈許，中窒之，虛石壙以待周太后，其隧獨通，而奉先殿祭，亦不設后主。

translations.literal: In the ninth month she was interred jointly at Yuling in separate burial passages; several zhang from Emperor Yingzong's inner chamber, the middle was blocked up, leaving an empty stone chamber to await Empress Dowager Zhou; her passage alone remained open, yet at sacrifices in the Hall of Ancestors no seat was set for the empress.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month she was buried with Yingzong at Yuling in separate vaults. A few yards from the late emperor's burial chamber, the middle section was sealed off, leaving an empty stone niche for Empress Dowager Zhou; only her passage remained open. Even so, no seat for the empress was provided at sacrifices in the Hall of Ancestors.

sentences.zh: 弘治十七年，周太后崩。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Hongzhi, Empress Dowager Zhou died.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of the Hongzhi reign, Empress Dowager Zhou died.

sentences.zh: 孝宗御便殿，出裕陵圖，示大學士劉健、謝遷、李東陽曰：「陵有二隧，若者窒，若者可通往來，皆先朝內臣所為，此未合禮。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaozong held court in the side hall, produced the plan of Yuling, and showed it to Grand Secretaries Liu Jian, Xie Qian, and Li Dongyang, saying: "The tomb has two passages—one blocked, one allowing passage back and forth. All were the work of inner-court eunuchs of the previous reign; this does not accord with ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozong held audience in a side hall, brought out the plan of Yuling, and showed Grand Secretaries Liu Jian, Xie Qian, and Li Dongyang the design. "The tomb has two passages," he said, "one sealed shut and one left open for access between them. All of this was done by eunuchs of the previous reign, and it does not accord with ritual.

sentences.zh: 昨​​見成化間彭時、姚夔等章奏，先朝大臣為國如此，先帝亦不得已耳。

translations.literal: Yesterday I saw the memorials of Peng Shi, Yao Kui, and others from the Chenghua period; the great ministers of the previous reign served the state in this way, and the late emperor had no choice.
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday I read the memorials submitted during the Chenghua reign by Peng Shi, Yao Kui, and others. The great ministers of the previous reign had served the state as best they could, and my late father had no real choice in the matter.

sentences.zh: 欽天監言通隧上干先帝陵堂，恐動地脈，朕已面折之。

translations.literal: The Directorate of Astronomy said that opening the passage would impinge upon the late emperor's burial chamber and might disturb the earth's veins; I have already refuted this to their faces.
translations.idiomatic: The Directorate of Astronomy claimed that opening the passage would violate the late emperor's burial chamber and disturb the earth's geomantic currents. I have already refuted this to their faces.

sentences.zh: 窒則天地閉塞，通則風氣流行。」

translations.literal: If blocked, heaven and earth are closed off; if opened, wind and qi circulate."
translations.idiomatic: If the passage is sealed, heaven and earth are shut off; if it is opened, wind and vital energy can flow."

sentences.zh: 健等因力贊。

translations.literal: Jian and the others thereupon strongly endorsed this.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jian and the others thereupon strongly endorsed the emperor's view.

sentences.zh: 帝復問祔廟禮，健等言：「祔二后，自唐始也。

translations.literal: The emperor again asked about the rites of enshrinement in the temple. Jian and the others said: "Enshrining two empresses began in the Tang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again asked about the rites for enshrining an empress in the ancestral temple. Liu Jian and the others replied, "Enshrining two empresses with one emperor began in the Tang dynasty.

sentences.zh: 祔三后，自宋始也，漢以前一帝一后。

translations.literal: Enshrining three empresses began in the Song; before the Han there was one emperor and one empress.
translations.idiomatic: Enshrining three empresses began in the Song. Before the Han, one emperor had one empress.

sentences.zh: 曩者定議合祔，孝莊太后居左，今大行太皇太后居右，且引唐、宋故事為證，臣等以此不敢复論。」

translations.literal: Previously it was decided that they should be enshrined together, with Empress Dowager Xiaozhuang on the left and the recently deceased Grand Empress Dowager on the right, and Tang and Song precedents were cited in proof; we ministers therefore dare not reopen the question."
translations.idiomatic: It was previously decided that they should be enshrined together, with Empress Dowager Xiaozhuang on the left and the late Grand Empress Dowager on the right, and Tang and Song precedents were cited in support. For that reason we dare not reopen the debate."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「二后已非，況復三后！」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Two empresses is already wrong—how much more three!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Two empresses is already improper—how much more so three!"

sentences.zh: 遷曰：「宋祔三后，一繼立，一​​生母也。」

translations.literal: Qian said: "In the Song, when three empresses were enshrined, one was a successor empress and one was the birth mother."
translations.idiomatic: Xie Qian said, "When the Song enshrined three empresses, one was a successor empress and one was the emperor's birth mother."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「事須師古，太皇太后鞠育朕躬，朕豈敢忘？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Matters must follow antiquity. The Grand Empress Dowager nurtured and raised my person—how could I forget?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "We must take antiquity as our guide. The Grand Empress Dowager raised me herself—how could I forget her?

sentences.zh: 顧私情耳。

translations.literal: It is only private feeling.
translations.idiomatic: That is only private feeling.

sentences.zh: 祖宗來，一帝一后。

translations.literal: Since our ancestors, one emperor and one empress.
translations.idiomatic: From the time of our ancestors, one emperor had one empress.

sentences.zh: 今並祔，壞禮自朕始。

translations.literal: Now to enshrine them together—ruining ritual begins with me.
translations.idiomatic: To enshrine them together now would mean that the ruin of ritual begins with me.

sentences.zh: 且奉先殿祭皇祖，特座一飯一匙而已。

translations.literal: Moreover, in sacrifices at the Hall of Ancestors to the imperial forebear, there is only a special seat with one serving of rice and one spoon.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when the imperial forebear is sacrificed to in the Hall of Ancestors, the empress receives only a separate seat with a single portion of rice and one spoon.

sentences.zh: 夫孝穆皇太后，朕生母也，別祀之奉慈殿。

translations.literal: As for Empress Dowager Xiaomu, she is my birth mother; she is separately worshipped in the Hall of Filial Kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Xiaomu is my birth mother, and she is worshipped separately in the Hall of Filial Kindness.

sentences.zh: 今仁壽宮前殿稍寬，朕欲奉太皇太后於此，他日奉孝穆皇太后於后，歲時祭享，如太廟。」

translations.literal: Now the front hall of Renshou Palace is somewhat spacious; I wish to install the Grand Empress Dowager here, and on another day install Empress Dowager Xiaomu behind her, with seasonal sacrifices as at the Imperial Ancestral Temple."
translations.idiomatic: The front hall of Renshou Palace is now somewhat spacious. I wish to install the Grand Empress Dowager there, and later install Empress Dowager Xiaomu behind her, with seasonal sacrifices conducted as at the Imperial Ancestral Temple."

sentences.zh: 於是命群臣詳議。

translations.literal: Thereupon he ordered the assembled ministers to deliberate in detail.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered the ministers to submit detailed recommendations.

sentences.zh: 議上，將建新廟，欽天監奏年方有礙。

translations.literal: When the deliberations were submitted, a new temple was to be built, but the Directorate of Astronomy reported that the year was inauspicious.
translations.idiomatic: When their recommendations were submitted, plans were made to build a new temple, but the Directorate of Astronomy reported that the year was inauspicious for construction.

sentences.zh: 廷議請暫祀周太后於奉慈殿，稱孝肅太皇太后。

translations.literal: Court deliberation requested temporarily worshipping Empress Dowager Zhou in the Hall of Filial Kindness, with the title Grand Empress Dowager Xiaosu.
translations.idiomatic: The court recommended temporarily worshipping Empress Dowager Zhou in the Hall of Filial Kindness under the title Grand Empress Dowager Xiaosu.

sentences.zh: 殿在奉先殿西，帝以祀孝穆，至是中奉孝肅而徙孝穆居左焉。

translations.literal: The hall is west of the Hall of Ancestors; the emperor had used it to worship Xiaomu, but now Xiaosu was placed in the center and Xiaomu was moved to the left.
translations.idiomatic: The hall stands west of the Hall of Ancestors. The emperor had used it to worship Xiaomu; now Xiaosu was placed in the center and Xiaomu was moved to the left.

sentences.zh: 帝始欲通隧，亦以陰陽家言，不果行。

translations.literal: The emperor had at first wished to open the passage, but because of the yin-yang masters' words, this was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had initially wished to open the burial passage, but because of the geomancers' warnings, the plan was not carried out.

sentences.zh: 孝肅周太后，英宗妃，憲宗生母也，昌平人。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Xiaosu Zhou, consort of Emperor Yingzong and birth mother of Emperor Xianzong, was a native of Changping.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Xiaosu of the Zhou clan, consort of Emperor Yingzong and birth mother of Emperor Xianzong, was a native of Changping.

sentences.zh: 天順元年封貴妃。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianshun she was enfeoffed as Noble Consort.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Tianshun reign she was enfeoffed as Noble Consort.

sentences.zh: 憲宗即位，尊為皇太后。

translations.literal: When Xianzong ascended the throne, she was honored as Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzong ascended the throne, she was honored as Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 其年十月，太后誕日，帝令僧道建齋祭。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of that year, on the empress dowager's birthday, the emperor ordered Buddhist and Daoist clergy to hold fasting rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of that year, on the empress dowager's birthday, the emperor ordered Buddhist and Daoist clergy to perform fasting rites.

sentences.zh: 禮部尚書姚夔帥群臣詣齋所，為太后祈福。

translations.literal: Minister of Rites Yao Kui led the assembled ministers to the fasting hall to pray for blessings for the empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Rites Yao Kui led the assembled ministers to the fasting hall to pray for the empress dowager's blessings.

sentences.zh: 給事中張寧等劾之。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Zhang Ning and others impeached this.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Zhang Ning and others impeached the practice.

sentences.zh: 帝是其言，令自后僧道齋醮，百官不得行香。

translations.literal: The emperor agreed with their words and ordered that henceforth, for Buddhist and Daoist fasting rites, officials were not to attend to burn incense.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and ordered that henceforth, at Buddhist and Daoist fasting rites, officials were not to attend to burn incense.

sentences.zh: 二十三年四月上徽號曰「聖慈仁壽皇太后」。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the twenty-third year a honorific title was conferred: "Grand Empress Dowager Shengci Renshou."
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the twenty-third year of his reign she was given the honorific title "Grand Empress Dowager Shengci Renshou."

sentences.zh: 孝宗立，尊為太皇太后。

translations.literal: When Xiaozong was enthroned, she was honored as Grand Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozong was enthroned, she was honored as Grand Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 先是，憲宗在位，事太后至孝，五日一朝，燕享必親。太后意所欲，惟恐不歡。至錢太后合葬裕陵，太后殊難之。憲宗委曲寬譬，乃得請。孝宗生西宮，母妃紀氏薨，太后育之宮中，省視萬方。及孝宗即位，事太后亦至孝。太后病瘍，久之愈，誥諭群臣曰：「自英皇厭代，予正位長樂，憲宗皇帝以天下養，二十四年猶一日。茲予偶患瘍，皇帝夜籲天，為予請命，春郊罷宴，問視惟勤，俾老年疾體，獲底康寧。以昔視今，父子兩世，孝同一揆，予甚嘉焉。」

translations.literal: Before this, while Xianzong was on the throne, he served the empress dowager with the utmost filial devotion, attending court with her once every five days and personally attending every banquet and feast. Whatever the empress dowager wished, he feared only that she might not be pleased. When it came to burying Empress Dowager Qian together in Yuling, the empress dowager found it especially difficult. Xianzong explained gently and at length, and only then obtained her consent. Xiaozong was born in the Western Palace, and when his mother Consort Ji died, the empress dowager raised him in the palace, looking after him in every way. When Xiaozong took the throne, he too served the empress dowager with the utmost filial devotion. The empress dowager suffered from an ulcer; after a long time it healed, and she issued an announcement to the assembled ministers: "Since the Ying Emperor passed from the age and I took my proper place in Changle Palace, Emperor Xianzong supported me with all under Heaven, twenty-four years as if they were one day. Recently I happened to suffer from an ulcer, and the emperor cried to Heaven by night, asking that my life be spared; he cancelled the spring suburban banquet, and his inquiries and visits were diligent, so that my aged and ailing body was able to reach health and peace. Comparing the past with the present, father and son over two generations have had the same measure of filial devotion, and I am deeply pleased."
translations.idiomatic: Before this, while Xianzong was on the throne, he served the empress dowager with utmost filial devotion, attending her once every five days and personally appearing at every banquet and feast. Whatever she wished, he feared only that she might not be pleased. When the question arose of burying Empress Dowager Qian together in Yuling, the empress dowager found it especially hard to accept. Xianzong explained gently and at length, and only then won her consent. Xiaozong was born in the Western Palace; after his mother, Consort Ji, died, the empress dowager raised him in the palace and looked after him in every way. When Xiaozong ascended the throne, he too served her with utmost filial devotion. The empress dowager suffered from an ulcer, and after a long time recovered. She then announced to the assembled ministers, "Since the Ying Emperor passed away and I took my proper place in Changle Palace, Emperor Xianzong supported me with the resources of the whole realm, twenty-four years as if they were one day. Recently I happened to suffer from an ulcer, and the emperor cried to Heaven by night, asking that my life be spared. He cancelled the spring suburban banquet and visited and asked after me diligently, allowing my old and ailing body to regain health and peace. Comparing the past with the present, father and son across two generations have shown the same measure of filial devotion, and I am deeply pleased."

sentences.zh: 弘治十一年冬，清寧宮災，太后移居仁壽宮。

translations.literal: In the winter of the eleventh year of Hongzhi, Qingning Palace burned; the empress dowager moved to Renshou Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the eleventh year of the Hongzhi reign, Qingning Palace burned down, and the empress dowager moved to Renshou Palace.

sentences.zh: 明年，清寧宮成，乃還居焉。

translations.literal: The next year, when Qingning Palace was completed, she returned to reside there.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, when Qingning Palace was rebuilt, she returned to live there.

sentences.zh: 太后弟長寧伯彧家有賜田，有司請厘正之，帝未許也，太后曰：「奈何以我故骫皇帝法！」

translations.literal: The empress dowager's younger brother, Changning Earl Yu, possessed granted fields at home; the officials requested their rectification, and the emperor had not yet assented, when the empress dowager said: "How can I, for my sake, bend the emperor's law!"
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager's younger brother, Changning Earl Yu, held imperial grant lands in his household. When officials requested that the holdings be corrected, the emperor had not yet consented, but the empress dowager said, "How can I, for my sake, bend the emperor's law!"

sentences.zh: 使歸地於官。

translations.literal: She had the land returned to the state.
translations.idiomatic: She had the land returned to the state.

sentences.zh: 弘治十七年三月崩，諡孝肅貞順康懿光烈輔天承聖睿皇后，合葬裕陵。

translations.literal: In the third month of the seventeenth year of Hongzhi she died; her posthumous title was Empress Xiaosu Zhenshun Kangyi Guanglie Futian Chengsheng Rui; she was interred jointly at Yuling.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the seventeenth year of the Hongzhi reign she died. She was given the posthumous title Empress Xiaosu Zhenshun Kangyi Guanglie Futian Chengsheng Rui and buried with Yingzong at Yuling.

sentences.zh: 以大學士劉健、謝遷、李東陽議，別祀於奉慈殿，不祔廟，仍稱太皇太后。

translations.literal: On the recommendation of Grand Secretaries Liu Jian, Xie Qian, and Li Dongyang, she was separately worshipped in the Hall of Filial Kindness, not enshrined in the temple, and still styled Grand Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: On the recommendation of Grand Secretaries Liu Jian, Xie Qian, and Li Dongyang, she was worshipped separately in the Hall of Filial Kindness rather than enshrined in the ancestral temple, and was still styled Grand Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十五年，與紀、邵二太后並移祀陵殿，題主曰「皇后」，不繫帝諡​​，以別嫡庶。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Jiajing, together with Empresses Dowager Ji and Shao she was moved to worship at the tomb hall; the spirit tablet was inscribed "Empress," without attaching the emperor's posthumous title, to distinguish principal from secondary wives.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of the Jiajing reign, she was moved together with Empresses Dowager Ji and Shao to worship at the tomb hall. The spirit tablet was inscribed simply "Empress," without the emperor's posthumous title, to distinguish principal from secondary consorts.

sentences.zh: 其后穆宗母孝恪、神宗母孝定、光宗母孝靖、熹宗母孝和、莊烈帝母孝純，咸遵用其制。

translations.literal: Thereafter the birth mothers Xiaoke of Muzong, Xiaoding of Shenzong, Xiaojing of Guangzong, Xiaohe of Xizong, and Xiaochun of the Chonglie Emperor all followed this system.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the birth mothers of Muzong, Shenzong, Guangzong, Xizong, and the Chonglie Emperor—respectively Xiaoke, Xiaoding, Xiaojing, Xiaohe, and Xiaochun—all followed this arrangement.

sentences.zh: 景帝廢后汪氏，順天人。

translations.literal: Deposed Empress Wang of Emperor Jing, a native of Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: Deposed Empress Wang of Emperor Jing, a native of Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 正統十年冊為郕王妃。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Zhengtong she was invested as consort of the Prince of Fu.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of the Zhengtong reign she was invested as consort of the Prince of Fu.

sentences.zh: 十四年冬，王即皇帝位，冊為皇后。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fourteenth year, when the prince ascended the throne, she was invested as empress.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the fourteenth year, when the prince took the throne, she was invested as empress.

sentences.zh: 后有賢德，嘗念京師諸死事及老弱遇害者暴骨原野，令官校掩埋之。

translations.literal: The empress had worthy virtue; she often thought of those who had died in service around the capital and the old and weak who had perished, their bones exposed in the wilds, and ordered officials and guards to bury them.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was a woman of worthy character. Mindful of those who had died in the capital's defense and of the old and weak left slain in the fields, she ordered officials and guards to gather and bury the exposed bones.

sentences.zh: 生二女，無子。

translations.literal: She bore two daughters and had no son.
translations.idiomatic: She bore two daughters and had no son.

sentences.zh: 景泰三年，妃杭氏生子見濟，景帝欲立為太子，而廢憲宗，后執不可。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jingtai, Consort Hang bore a son, Jianji; Emperor Jing wished to install him as heir apparent and depose Xianzong, but the empress firmly refused.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Jingtai reign, Consort Hang bore a son, Jianji. Emperor Jing wished to make the boy heir apparent and depose Xianzong, but the empress firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 以是忤帝意，遂廢后，立杭氏為皇后。

translations.literal: Because of this she offended the emperor's wishes; the empress was thereupon deposed and Consort Hang was installed as empress.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this she offended the emperor, who deposed her and installed Consort Hang as empress.

sentences.zh: 七年，杭后崩，諡肅孝。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Empress Hang died; her posthumous title was Su Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of his reign Empress Hang died and was given the posthumous title Su Xiao.

sentences.zh: 英宗復位，削皇后號，毀所葬陵，而后仍稱郕王妃。

translations.literal: When Yingzong regained the throne, the empress's title was stripped, her tomb destroyed, and she was again styled consort of the Prince of Fu.
translations.idiomatic: When Yingzong regained the throne, her title as empress was revoked, her tomb was destroyed, and she was again styled consort of the Prince of Fu.

sentences.zh: 景帝崩，英宗以其后宮唐氏等殉，議及后。

translations.literal: When Jing died, Yingzong had the women of his inner palace, such as Lady Tang, follow him in death; the discussion extended to the empress.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing died, Yingzong ordered the women of his inner palace, including Lady Tang, to follow him in death, and the discussion extended to the former empress as well.

sentences.zh: 李賢曰：「妃已幽廢，況兩女幼，尤可憫。」

translations.literal: Li Xian said: "The consort has already been confined and deposed; moreover her two daughters are young—this is especially pitiable."
translations.idiomatic: Li Xian said, "The consort has already been confined in disgrace, and her two daughters are still young—she is especially to be pitied."

sentences.zh: 帝乃已。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon desisted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thereupon desisted.

sentences.zh: 憲宗復立為太子，雅知后不欲廢立，事之甚恭。

translations.literal: When Xianzong was reinstated as heir apparent, he well knew that the empress had not wished the change of heir, and served her with great respect.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzong was reinstated as heir apparent, he knew well that the empress had opposed the change of succession, and he treated her with great respect.

sentences.zh: 因為帝言，遷之外王府，得盡攜宮中所有而出。

translations.literal: He therefore spoke to the emperor, and she was moved to an outer princely residence, allowed to take out everything she possessed in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore spoke to the emperor on her behalf, and she was moved to an outer princely residence, permitted to take with her everything she possessed in the palace.

sentences.zh: 與周太后相得甚歡，歲時入宮，敘家人禮。

translations.literal: She got on extremely well with Empress Dowager Zhou, entering the palace at the seasons to observe family rites.
translations.idiomatic: She got on extremely well with Empress Dowager Zhou, visiting the palace at the proper seasons to observe family courtesies.

sentences.zh: 然性剛執。

translations.literal: Yet her nature was firm and unyielding.
translations.idiomatic: Yet her nature was firm and unyielding.

sentences.zh: 一日，英宗問太監劉桓曰：「記有玉玲瓏系腰，今何在？」

translations.literal: One day Yingzong asked the eunuch Liu Huan: "I recall a jade linglong worn at the waist—where is it now?"
translations.idiomatic: One day Yingzong asked the eunuch Liu Huan, "I recall a jade ornament called linglong worn at the waist—where is it now?"

sentences.zh: 桓言當在妃所。

translations.literal: Huan said it should be with the consort.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Huan said it should be in the consort's possession.

sentences.zh: 英宗命索之。

translations.literal: Yingzong ordered it sought.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzong ordered it sought out.

sentences.zh: 后投諸井，對使者曰：「無之。」

translations.literal: The empress threw it into a well and said to the envoy: "It is not here."
translations.idiomatic: The empress threw it into a well and told the envoy, "It is not here."

sentences.zh: 已而告人曰：「七年天子，不堪消受此數片玉耶！」

translations.literal: Later she told others: "Seven years an emperor—can he not bear to consume these few pieces of jade!"
translations.idiomatic: Later she told others, "He was emperor for seven years—can he not bear to keep these few pieces of jade!"

sentences.zh: 已，有言后出所攜鉅萬計，英宗遣使檢取之，遂立盡。

translations.literal: Soon afterward it was said that when the empress departed she had taken out riches numbering in the tens of thousands; Yingzong sent envoys to inspect and seize them, and her property was exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Before long it was reported that when the empress left the palace she had taken out wealth amounting to tens of thousands; Yingzong sent envoys to inspect and seize it, and her possessions were exhausted.

sentences.zh: 正德元年十二月薨，議祭葬禮。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the first year of Zhengde she died; the rites of sacrifice and burial were deliberated.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the first year of the Zhengde reign she died, and the rites of sacrifice and burial were deliberated.

sentences.zh: 大學士王鏊曰：「葬以妃，祭以后。」

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Wang Ao said: "Burial according to the rites for a consort, sacrifice according to the rites for an empress."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Wang Ao said, "Let her be buried with the rites due a consort, but sacrificed to with the rites due an empress."

sentences.zh: 遂合葬金山。

translations.literal: Thereupon she was interred jointly at Jinshan.
translations.idiomatic: She was then buried at Jinshan accordingly.

sentences.zh: 明年上尊諡曰「貞惠安和景皇后」。

translations.literal: The next year a posthumous honorific title was conferred: "Empress Zhenhui Anhe Jing."
translations.idiomatic: The following year she was given the posthumous title "Empress Zhenhui Anhe Jing."

sentences.zh: 憲宗廢后吳氏，順天人。

translations.literal: Deposed Empress Wu of Emperor Xianzong, a native of Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: Deposed Empress Wu of Emperor Xianzong, a native of Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 天順八年七月立為皇后。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the eighth year of Tianshun she was installed as empress.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the eighth year of the Tianshun reign she was installed as empress.

sentences.zh: 先是，憲宗居東宮，萬貴妃已擅寵。

translations.literal: Earlier, while Xianzong resided in the Eastern Palace, Lady Wan had already monopolized favor.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Xianzong was crown prince, Lady Wan had already monopolized the emperor's favor.

sentences.zh: 后既立，摘其過，杖之。

translations.literal: After the empress was installed, she seized upon Wan's faults and had her beaten.
translations.idiomatic: After the empress was installed, she seized upon Lady Wan's faults and had her beaten.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，下詔曰：「先帝為朕簡求賢淑，已定王氏，育於別宮待期。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and issued an edict saying: "The late emperor selected a worthy and virtuous consort for me and had already fixed upon Lady Wang, rearing her in a separate palace until the appointed time.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged and issued an edict: "The late emperor selected a worthy and virtuous consort for me and had already chosen Lady Wang, rearing her in a separate palace until the appointed time.

sentences.zh: 太監牛玉輒以選退吳氏於太后前複選。

translations.literal: The eunuch Niu Yu presumptuously brought back the rejected Lady Wu before the empress dowager for reselection.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Niu Yu presumptuously brought the rejected Lady Wu back before the empress dowager for reselection.

sentences.zh: 冊立禮成之后，朕見舉動輕佻，禮度率略，德不稱位，因察其實，始知非預立者。

translations.literal: After the investiture rites were completed, I saw her conduct was frivolous and her ritual deportment careless; her virtue did not match her rank. Upon investigating the facts, I learned she was not the one originally chosen.
translations.idiomatic: After the investiture rites were completed, I found her conduct frivolous and her deportment careless, her virtue unworthy of her rank. Upon investigation I learned she was not the woman originally chosen.

sentences.zh: 用是不得已，請命太后，廢吳氏別宮。」

translations.literal: For this reason, having no choice, I requested the empress dowager's command and deposed Lady Wu to a separate palace."
translations.idiomatic: For this reason, having no choice, I requested the empress dowager's command and deposed Lady Wu to a separate palace."

sentences.zh: 立甫踰月耳。

translations.literal: She had been installed for barely more than a month.
translations.idiomatic: She had been empress for barely a month.

sentences.zh: 后父​​俊，先授都督同知，至是下獄戍邊。

translations.literal: The empress's father Jun had earlier been appointed Vice Commissioner-in-chief; at this time he was imprisoned and sent to guard the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: The empress's father, Jun, had earlier been appointed Vice Commissioner-in-chief; now he was imprisoned and sent to guard the frontier.

sentences.zh: 謫玉孝陵種菜，玉從子太常少卿綸、甥吏部員外郎楊琮並除名，姻家懷寧侯孫鏜閒住。

translations.literal: Yu was demoted to grow vegetables at the Xiaoling tomb; Yu's nephew Vice Minister of Rites Lun and his nephew by marriage, Department Vice Director Yang Cong, were both struck from the rolls; his affinal connection, Marquis of Huaining Sun Tang, was ordered to live in retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Yu was demoted to grow vegetables at the Xiaoling tomb. Yu's nephew, Vice Minister of Rites Lun, and his nephew by marriage, Department Vice Director Yang Cong, were both struck from the rolls; his affinal connection, Marquis of Huaining Sun Tang, was ordered to live in retirement.

sentences.zh: 於是南京給事中王徽、王淵、朱寬、李翱、李鈞等合疏言玉罪重罰輕，因並劾大學士李賢。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Nanjing supervising secretaries Wang Hui, Wang Yuan, Zhu Kuan, Li Ao, Li Jun, and others jointly memorialized that Yu's crime was grave and his punishment light, and also impeached Grand Secretary Li Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the Nanjing supervising secretaries Wang Hui, Wang Yuan, Zhu Kuan, Li Ao, Li Jun, and others jointly memorialized that Niu Yu's crime was grave and his punishment too light, and also impeached Grand Secretary Li Xian.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，徽等皆貶邊州判官。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry, and Hui and the others were all demoted to magistrates of frontier prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged, and Wang Hui and the others were all demoted to magistrates of frontier prefectures.

sentences.zh: 后孝宗生於西宮，后保抱惟謹。

translations.literal: Empress Xiaozong was born in the Western Palace; the empress nursed and tended him with utmost care.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozong was born in the Western Palace, and the empress nursed and tended him with the utmost care.

sentences.zh: 孝宗即位，念后恩，命服膳皆如母后禮，官其侄錦衣百戶。

translations.literal: When Xiaozong ascended the throne, mindful of the empress's kindness, he ordered that her food and clothing be treated with the rites due a mother empress, and appointed her nephew a commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozong ascended the throne, mindful of the empress's kindness, he ordered that her food and clothing be provided with the rites due a mother empress, and appointed her nephew a commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 正德四年薨。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhengde she died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of the Zhengde reign she died.

sentences.zh: 劉瑾欲焚之。

translations.literal: Liu Jin wished to burn her body.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jin wished to have her body burned.

sentences.zh: 大學士王鏊持不可，乃以妃禮葬。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Wang Ao held that this could not be done, and she was buried with the rites due a consort.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Wang Ao objected, and she was buried with the rites due a consort.

sentences.zh: 孝貞皇后王氏，上元人。

translations.literal: Empress Xiaozhen Wang, a native of Shangyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xiaozhen of the Wang clan, a native of Shangyuan.

sentences.zh: 憲宗在東宮，英宗為擇配，得十二人，選后及吳氏、柏氏留宮中。

translations.literal: While Xianzong was in the Eastern Palace, Yingzong chose a match for him, obtaining twelve women; the empress, Lady Wu, and Lady Bo were selected to remain in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: While Xianzong was crown prince, Yingzong chose a match for him from twelve candidates; the future empress, Lady Wu, and Lady Bo were selected to remain in the palace.

sentences.zh: 吳氏既立而廢，遂冊為皇后，天順八年十月也。

translations.literal: After Lady Wu was installed and then deposed, she was thereupon invested as empress—in the tenth month of the eighth year of Tianshun.
translations.idiomatic: After Lady Wu was installed and then deposed, she was invested as empress in the tenth month of the eighth year of the Tianshun reign.

sentences.zh: 萬貴妃寵冠后宮，后處之淡如。

translations.literal: Lady Wan's favor topped the inner palace; the empress treated this with indifference.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wan's favor surpassed all others in the inner palace, but the empress treated the matter with indifference.

sentences.zh: 孝宗即位，尊為皇太后。

translations.literal: When Xiaozong ascended the throne, she was honored as Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozong ascended the throne, she was honored as Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 武宗即位，尊為太皇太后。

translations.literal: When Wuzong ascended the throne, she was honored as Grand Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuzong ascended the throne, she was honored as Grand Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 正德五年十二月上尊號曰慈聖康壽。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the fifth year of Zhengde a honorific title was conferred: Cisheng Kangshou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the fifth year of the Zhengde reign she was given the honorific title Cisheng Kangshou.

sentences.zh: 十三年二月崩，上尊諡曰「孝貞莊懿恭靖仁慈欽天輔聖純皇后」，合葬茂陵，祔太廟。

translations.literal: In the second month of the thirteenth year she died; a posthumous honorific title was conferred: "Empress Xiaozhen Zhuangyi Gongjing Ciren Qintian Fusheng Chun," and she was interred jointly at Maoling and enshrined in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the thirteenth year of his reign she died. She was given the posthumous title "Empress Xiaozhen Zhuangyi Gongjing Ciren Qintian Fusheng Chun," buried with Xianzong at Maoling, and enshrined in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 孝穆紀太后，孝宗生母也，賀縣人。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Xiaomu Ji, birth mother of Xiaozong, was a native of He County.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Xiaomu of the Ji clan, birth mother of Emperor Xiaozong, was a native of He County.

sentences.zh: 本蠻土官女。

translations.literal: Originally the daughter of a tribal chieftain.
translations.idiomatic: She was originally the daughter of a tribal chieftain.

sentences.zh: 成化中徵蠻，俘入掖庭，授女史，警敏通文字，命守內藏。

translations.literal: In the Chenghua period, when the tribes were attacked, she was captured and entered the inner palace; she was appointed a female scribe, alert and clever and versed in writing, and ordered to guard the inner treasury.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chenghua reign, when the tribes were attacked, she was captured and sent to the inner palace. Appointed a female scribe, she was quick-witted and literate, and was ordered to guard the inner treasury.

sentences.zh: 時萬貴妃專寵而妒，后宮有娠者皆治使墮。

translations.literal: At that time Honored Consort Wan held exclusive favor and was jealous; any woman in the inner palace who became pregnant was subjected to treatment to force miscarriage.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Honored Consort Wan enjoyed exclusive favor and was fiercely jealous; any woman in the inner palace who conceived was forced to abort.

sentences.zh: 柏賢妃生悼恭太子，亦為所害。

translations.literal: Consort Bo the Virtuous gave birth to the Diligent and Reverent Crown Prince, and she too was harmed by her.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Bo the Virtuous bore the Diligent and Reverent Crown Prince, and she too was destroyed by Wan.

sentences.zh: 帝偶行內藏，應對稱旨，悅，幸之，遂有身。

translations.literal: The emperor happened to pass through the inner storehouse; she answered with such aptness that he was pleased, favored her, and she conceived.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor happened to pass through the inner storehouse; her replies pleased him, he favored her, and she became pregnant.

sentences.zh: 萬貴妃知而恚甚，令婢鉤治之。

translations.literal: When Honored Consort Wan learned of it she was furious and ordered a servant girl to procure treatment for her.
translations.idiomatic: When Honored Consort Wan learned of this she was enraged and ordered a maid to obtain abortifacients for her.

sentences.zh: 婢謬報曰病痞。

translations.literal: The servant falsely reported that she was afflicted with abdominal bloating.
translations.idiomatic: The maid falsely reported that she suffered from abdominal distension.

sentences.zh: 乃謫居安樂堂。

translations.literal: She was then relegated to reside at the Hall of Peaceful Joy.
translations.idiomatic: She was then banished to live in the Hall of Peaceful Joy.

sentences.zh: 久之，生孝宗，使門監張敏溺焉。

translations.literal: After a long time she gave birth to Xiaozong; a palace gate eunuch named Zhang Min was ordered to drown the child.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while she gave birth to Xiaozong, and the gate eunuch Zhang Min was ordered to drown the infant.

sentences.zh: 敏驚曰：「上未有子，奈何棄之。」

translations.literal: Min was startled and said: "The sovereign has no son yet—how can we abandon him?"
translations.idiomatic: Min was horrified and said, "Your Majesty has no son yet—how can we cast him away?"

sentences.zh: 稍哺粉餌飴蜜，藏之他室，貴妃日伺無所得。

translations.literal: He gave the child gruel mixed with honey to suckle, hid him in another chamber, and the honored consort watched daily but found nothing.
translations.idiomatic: He fed the child gruel sweetened with honey, hid him in another room, and the honored consort watched every day but discovered nothing.

sentences.zh: 至五六歲，未敢剪胎髮。

translations.literal: Until the boy was five or six years old, they did not dare cut his fetal hair.
translations.idiomatic: Until the boy was five or six, they did not dare cut his hair.

sentences.zh: 時吳后廢居西內，近安樂堂，密知其事，往來哺養，帝不知也。

translations.literal: At that time the deposed Empress Wu lived in the Western Inner Palace near the Hall of Peaceful Joy; she secretly knew of the affair and came and went to nurse and raise the child—the emperor knew nothing of it.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the deposed Empress Wu lived in the Western Inner Palace near the Hall of Peaceful Joy; she secretly learned of the matter and went back and forth to nurse the child—the emperor knew nothing.

sentences.zh: 帝自悼恭太子薨后，久無嗣，中外皆以為憂。

translations.literal: Since the Diligent and Reverent Crown Prince's death, the emperor had long had no heir, and court and countryside alike were troubled by it.
translations.idiomatic: Since the death of the Diligent and Reverent Crown Prince, the emperor had long been without an heir, and both court and realm were deeply worried.

sentences.zh: 成化十一年，帝召張敏櫛發，照鏡歎曰：「老將至而無子。」

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Chenghua the emperor summoned Zhang Min to comb his hair; gazing into the mirror he sighed: "Old age approaches and I have no son."
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Chenghua the emperor summoned Zhang Min to comb his hair; looking in the mirror he sighed, "Old age is coming and I still have no son."

sentences.zh: 敏伏地曰：「死罪，萬歲已有子也。」

translations.literal: Min prostrated himself and said: "A capital crime—but Your Majesty already has a son."
translations.idiomatic: Min prostrated himself and said, "This is a capital offense—but Your Majesty already has a son."

sentences.zh: 帝愕然，問安在。

translations.literal: The emperor was stunned and asked where he was.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was astonished and asked where the boy was.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「奴言即死，萬歲當為皇子主。」

translations.literal: He replied: "If I speak and die, Your Majesty must stand as master to the prince."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "If I speak and must die, Your Majesty must act as the prince's protector."

sentences.zh: 於是太監懷恩頓首曰：「敏言是。

translations.literal: Thereupon the eunuch Huai En kowtowed and said: "Min speaks truly.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the eunuch Huai En kowtowed and said, "Min speaks the truth.

sentences.zh: 皇子潛養西內，今已六歲矣，匿不敢聞。」

translations.literal: The prince was secretly raised in the Western Inner Palace; he is six years old now—we hid this and dared not report it."
translations.idiomatic: The prince has been secretly raised in the Western Inner Palace; he is already six years old—we concealed this and dared not speak of it."

sentences.zh: 帝大喜，即日幸西內，遣使往迎皇子。

translations.literal: The emperor was overjoyed; that very day he visited the Western Inner Palace and sent envoys to fetch the prince.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was overjoyed; that same day he went to the Western Inner Palace and sent envoys to bring the prince.

sentences.zh: 使至，妃抱皇子泣曰：「兒去，吾不得生。

translations.literal: When the envoys arrived, the consort held the prince and wept: "When the child goes, I cannot live.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoys arrived, the consort embraced the prince and wept, "When my son leaves, I cannot survive.

sentences.zh: 兒見黃袍有須者，即兒父也。」

translations.literal: If the child sees a man in yellow robes with a beard, that is your father."
translations.idiomatic: If you see a bearded man in yellow robes, that is your father."

sentences.zh: 衣以小緋袍，乘小輿，擁至階下，髮披地，走投帝懷。

translations.literal: They dressed him in a small crimson robe, put him in a small palanquin, and escorted him to the foot of the steps; his hair trailing to the ground, he ran and threw himself into the emperor's arms.
translations.idiomatic: They dressed him in a small crimson robe, placed him in a small palanquin, and escorted him to the foot of the steps; his hair streaming to the ground, he ran and threw himself into the emperor's arms.

sentences.zh: 帝置之膝，撫視久之，悲喜泣下曰：「我子也，類我。」

translations.literal: The emperor set him on his knee, gazed and caressed him long, weeping with joy and sorrow: "My son—he resembles me."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor set him on his knee, gazed and caressed him for a long while, weeping with joy and grief: "My son—he looks like me."

sentences.zh: 使懷恩赴內閣具道其故。

translations.literal: He sent Huai En to the Grand Secretariat to relate the whole story in detail.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Huai En to the Grand Secretariat to explain the whole affair.

sentences.zh: 群臣皆大喜。

translations.literal: The assembled ministers were all greatly rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: All the ministers rejoiced greatly.

sentences.zh: 明日，入賀，頒詔天下。

translations.literal: The next day they entered to congratulate him, and an edict was proclaimed throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they entered to offer congratulations, and an edict was issued to the whole empire.

sentences.zh: 移妃居永壽宮，數召見。

translations.literal: The consort was moved to the Palace of Eternal Longevity and summoned frequently.
translations.idiomatic: The consort was moved to the Palace of Eternal Longevity and summoned often.

sentences.zh: 萬貴妃日夜怨泣曰：「群小紿我。」

translations.literal: Honored Consort Wan complained and wept day and night: "Those petty men deceived me."
translations.idiomatic: Honored Consort Wan complained and wept day and night, "Those petty men tricked me."

sentences.zh: 其年六月，妃暴薨。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of that year the consort died suddenly.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of that year the consort died suddenly.

sentences.zh: 或曰貴妃致之死，或曰自縊也。

translations.literal: Some say the honored consort caused her death; some say she hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: Some say the honored consort had her killed; others say she hanged herself.

sentences.zh: 諡「恭恪莊僖淑妃」。

translations.literal: Posthumous title: "Consort Gongke Zhuangxi Shu."
translations.idiomatic: She was given the posthumous title "Consort Gongke Zhuangxi Shu."

sentences.zh: 敏懼，亦吞金死。

translations.literal: Min, in fear, also swallowed gold and died.
translations.idiomatic: Min, terrified, also swallowed gold and died.

sentences.zh: 敏，同安人。

translations.literal: Min was a native of Tong'an.
translations.idiomatic: Min was a native of Tong'an.

sentences.zh: 孝宗既立為皇太子，時孝肅皇太后居仁壽宮，語帝曰：「以兒付我。」

translations.literal: Once Xiaozong was installed as crown prince, Empress Dowager Xiaosu resided at the Palace of Human Longevity and told the emperor: "Entrust the boy to me."
translations.idiomatic: After Xiaozong was made crown prince, Empress Dowager Xiaosu, residing at the Palace of Human Longevity, told the emperor, "Leave the boy with me."

sentences.zh: 太子遂居仁壽。

translations.literal: The crown prince then took up residence at Ren Shou.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince then lived at the Palace of Human Longevity.

sentences.zh: 一日，貴妃召太子食，孝肅謂太子曰：「兒去，無食也。」

translations.literal: One day the honored consort summoned the crown prince to dine; Xiaosu told the prince: "When you go, do not eat."
translations.idiomatic: One day the honored consort summoned the crown prince to dine; Xiaosu told him, "When you go, do not eat anything."

sentences.zh: 太子至，貴妃賜食，曰：「已飽。」

translations.literal: When the prince arrived, the honored consort offered food; he said: "I am already full."
translations.idiomatic: When the prince arrived, the honored consort offered him food; he said, "I am already full."

sentences.zh: 進羹，曰：「疑有毒。」

translations.literal: When soup was served, he said: "I suspect it is poisoned."
translations.idiomatic: When soup was brought, he said, "I fear it may be poisoned."

sentences.zh: 貴妃大恚曰：「是兒數歲即如是，他日魚肉我矣。」

translations.literal: The honored consort was furious: "At only a few years old this boy is already like this—when he grows up he will have me cut to pieces like fish and flesh."
translations.idiomatic: The honored consort was furious: "At only a few years old this child is already like this—when he grows up he will butcher me."

sentences.zh: 因恚而成疾。

translations.literal: She fell ill from rage.
translations.idiomatic: She fell ill from her fury.

sentences.zh: 孝宗即位，追諡淑妃為「孝穆慈慧恭恪莊僖崇天承聖純皇后」，遷葬茂陵，別祀奉慈殿。

translations.literal: When Xiaozong ascended the throne, he posthumously titled the consort as "Empress Xiaomu Cihui Gongke Zhuangxi Chongtian Chengsheng Chun," moved her burial to Maoling, and enshrined her separately at the Hall of Filial Reverence.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozong ascended the throne, he posthumously ennobled the consort as "Empress Xiaomu Cihui Gongke Zhuangxi Chongtian Chengsheng Chun," moved her burial to Maoling, and enshrined her separately in the Hall of Filial Reverence.

sentences.zh: 帝悲念太后，特遣太監蔡用求太后家，得紀父貴、紀祖旺兄弟以聞。

translations.literal: The emperor, grieving for the empress dowager, specially sent the eunuch Cai Yong to seek her family and found Ji Fugui and Ji Zuwang, brothers of the Ji clan, whom he reported.
translations.idiomatic: Grieving for the empress dowager, the emperor specially sent the eunuch Cai Yong to search for her family and found the brothers Ji Fugui and Ji Zuwang, whom he reported.

sentences.zh: 帝大喜，詔改「父貴」為「貴」，授錦衣衛指揮同知；

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and ordered that "Fugui" be changed to "Gui," appointing him Assistant Commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was overjoyed and ordered that "Fugui" be shortened to "Gui," appointing him Assistant Commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard;

sentences.zh: 「祖旺」為「旺」，授錦衣衛指揮僉事。

translations.literal: "Zuwang" to be changed to "Wang," appointing him Vice Commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: and "Zuwang" to "Wang," appointing him Vice Commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 賜予第宅、金帛、莊田、奴婢，不可勝計。

translations.literal: Mansions, gold, silks, estate lands, and servants were bestowed beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Mansions, gold, silks, estates, and servants were lavished on them beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 追贈太后父為中軍都督府左都督，母為夫人。

translations.literal: The empress dowager's father was posthumously honored as Left Commissioner of the Central Military Commission; her mother as Lady.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager's father was posthumously enfeoffed as Left Commissioner of the Central Military Commission, and her mother as Lady.

sentences.zh: 其曾祖、祖父亦如之。

translations.literal: Her great-grandfather and grandfather received like honors.
translations.idiomatic: Her great-grandfather and grandfather received comparable honors.

sentences.zh: 遣修太后先塋之在賀者，置守墳戶，復其家。

translations.literal: He dispatched workers to restore the empress dowager's ancestral graves in Hexian, posted tomb guardians, and exempted the family from labor service.
translations.idiomatic: He sent men to restore the empress dowager's ancestral graves in Hexian, posted guardians for the tombs, and restored the family's tax and labor exemptions.

sentences.zh: 先是，太后在宮中，嘗自言家賀縣，姓紀，幼不能知親族也。

translations.literal: Earlier, while in the palace, the empress dowager had said herself that her family was in Hexian County and surnamed Ji, but in childhood she could not know her kin.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while still in the palace, the empress dowager had said that her family was from Hexian County and surnamed Ji, but in childhood she had not known her relatives.

sentences.zh: 太監郭鏞聞而識之。

translations.literal: The eunuch Guo Yong heard this and took note.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Guo Yong heard this and remembered it.

sentences.zh: 太監陸愷者，亦廣西人，故姓李，蠻中紀、李同音，因妄稱太后兄，令人訪其族人詣京師。

translations.literal: The eunuch Lu Kai was also from Guangxi; formerly surnamed Li—in the tribal tongue Ji and Li were homophones—so he falsely claimed to be the empress dowager's elder brother and sent men to seek his clansmen to come to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Lu Kai was also from Guangxi and had formerly been surnamed Li; in the tribal languages Ji and Li sounded alike, so he falsely claimed to be the empress dowager's elder brother and sent men to find his clansmen and bring them to the capital.

sentences.zh: 愷女兄夫韋父成者出冒之，有司待以戚畹，名所居里曰迎恩里。

translations.literal: Kai's brother-in-law Wei Fucheng came forward to impersonate him; the officials treated him as imperial kin and named his neighborhood Reception of Grace Lane.
translations.idiomatic: Kai's brother-in-law Wei Fucheng stepped forward to impersonate the kin; the officials treated him as imperial relatives and named his neighborhood Reception of Grace Lane.

sentences.zh: 貴、旺曰：「韋猶冒李，況我實李氏。」

translations.literal: Gui and Wang said: "Wei merely impersonated the Lis—how much more are we actually of the Li clan."
translations.idiomatic: Gui and Wang said, "Wei only impersonated the Lis—how much more so should we, who are truly of the Li clan."

sentences.zh: 因詐為宗系上有司，有司莫辨也。

translations.literal: They falsified genealogies and submitted them to the officials, who could not distinguish truth from falsehood.
translations.idiomatic: They forged genealogies and submitted them to the officials, who could not tell what was true.

sentences.zh: 二人既驟貴，父成亦詣闕爭辨。

translations.literal: Once the two men had suddenly risen to wealth and rank, Fucheng also went to the court to dispute the claim.
translations.idiomatic: Once the two men had suddenly risen to wealth and rank, Fucheng also went to court to contest the claim.

sentences.zh: 帝命郭鏞按之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Guo Yong to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Guo Yong to investigate the matter.

sentences.zh: 鏞逐父成，猶令馳驛歸。

translations.literal: Yong drove Fucheng away but still had him escorted home by post relay.
translations.idiomatic: Yong drove Fucheng off but still had him sent home by courier relay.

sentences.zh: 及帝使治后先塋，蠻中李姓者數輩，皆稱太后家，自言於使者。

translations.literal: When the emperor sent men to tend the empress's ancestral graves, several men surnamed Li in the tribal lands all claimed to be the empress dowager's family and declared this to the envoys.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor sent men to restore the empress dowager's ancestral graves, several men surnamed Li in the tribal territories all claimed to be her kin and told the envoys so.

sentences.zh: 使者還，奏貴、旺不實。

translations.literal: The envoys returned and reported that Gui and Wang were not genuine.
translations.idiomatic: The envoys returned and reported that Gui and Wang were impostors.

sentences.zh: 復遣給事中孫珪、御史滕祐間行連、賀間，微服入瑤、僮中訪之，盡得其狀，歸奏。

translations.literal: He again sent Supervising Secretary Sun Gui and Censor Teng You to travel secretly between Lian and He, entering Yao and Zhuang lands in plain dress to inquire—they obtained the full circumstances and returned to report.
translations.idiomatic: He again sent Supervising Secretary Sun Gui and Censor Teng You to travel covertly through Lianzhou and Hezhou, entering Yao and Zhuang country in plain clothes to investigate; they learned the full truth and returned to report.

sentences.zh: 帝謫罰鏞等有差，戍貴、旺邊海。

translations.literal: The emperor punished Yong and others with varying demotions and exiled Gui and Wang to the coastal frontier.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor punished Yong and the others with varying penalties and exiled Gui and Wang to the coastal frontier.

sentences.zh: 自此帝數求太后家，竟不得。

translations.literal: From then on the emperor repeatedly sought the empress dowager's family but never found them.
