translations.idiomatic: From then on the emperor searched repeatedly for the empress dowager's family but never found them.

sentences.zh: 弘治三年，禮部尚書耿裕奏曰：「粵西當大徵之后，兵燹飢荒，人民奔竄，歲月悠遠，踪跡難明。

translations.literal: In the third year of Hongzhi, Minister of Rites Geng Yu memorialized: "Guangxi, after the great punitive campaign, suffered war, famine, and the flight of the people; years have passed and traces are hard to discern.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Hongzhi, Minister of Rites Geng Yu memorialized: "After the great campaign in western Guangdong, Guangxi endured war, famine, and mass flight; years have passed and traces are hard to find.

sentences.zh: 昔孝慈高皇后與高皇帝同起艱難，化家為國，徐王親高皇后父，當后之身，尋求家族，尚不克獲，然后立廟宿州，春秋祭祀。

translations.literal: In the past Empress Xiaoci Gao rose from hardship with the founding emperor and transformed family into state; Prince Xu, a kinsman of the empress's father, during the empress's lifetime sought her family but still could not obtain them—only then did they establish a temple at Suzhou with spring and autumn sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In the past Empress Xiaoci Gao and the founding emperor rose together through hardship and made a household into a dynasty; Prince Xu, a kinsman of the empress's father, sought her family while she still lived and could not find them—only then was a temple established at Suzhou with sacrifices in spring and autumn.

sentences.zh: 今紀太后幼離西粵，入侍先帝，連、賀非徐、宿中原之地，嬪宮無母后正位之年，陛下訪尋雖切，安從得其實哉！

translations.literal: Now Empress Dowager Ji left western Guangdong in childhood to serve the late emperor; Lian and He are not the central plains of Xu and Suzhou, and the inner palace had no years of the empress dowager in formal position—though Your Majesty's search is earnest, how can the truth be obtained!
translations.idiomatic: Now Empress Dowager Ji left western Guangdong as a child to serve the late emperor; Lianzhou and Hezhou are not the heartland of Xu and Suzhou, and she never held the empress's seat in the inner palace—though Your Majesty searches with all earnestness, how can the truth be recovered!

sentences.zh: 臣愚謂可仿徐王故事，定擬太后父母封號，立祠桂林致祭。」

translations.literal: I humbly propose following Prince Xu's precedent: fix posthumous titles for the empress dowager's parents and establish a shrine in Guilin for sacrifice."
translations.idiomatic: I humbly propose following Prince Xu's precedent: confer posthumous titles on the empress dowager's parents and establish a shrine in Guilin for sacrifice."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「孝穆皇太后早棄朕躬，每一思念，惄焉如割。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Empress Dowager Xiaomu left my person early; each time I think of her, the anguish is like being cut apart.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Empress Dowager Xiaomu left me too soon; each time I think of her, the pain is like being torn apart.

sentences.zh: 初謂宗親尚可旁求，寧受百欺，冀獲一是。

translations.literal: At first I thought kin might still be found through collateral search—I would rather be deceived a hundred times than fail to gain one truth.
translations.idiomatic: At first I thought her kin might still be found through wider search; I would rather be deceived a hundred times than miss one true relative.

sentences.zh: 卿等謂歲久無從物色，請加封立廟，以慰聖母之靈。

translations.literal: You say years have passed with no means to identify them, and request additional enfeoffment and a temple to comfort the holy mother's spirit.
translations.idiomatic: You say so many years have passed that they cannot be identified, and ask to enfeoff them and build a temple to comfort my mother's spirit.

sentences.zh: 皇祖既有故事，朕心雖不忍，又奚敢違。」

translations.literal: The imperial grandfather already set a precedent; though my heart is unwilling, how dare I disobey."
translations.idiomatic: The imperial grandfather already established a precedent; though my heart cannot bear it, how dare I disobey?"

sentences.zh: 於是封后父推誠宣力武臣特進光祿大夫柱國慶元伯，諡端僖，后母伯夫人，立廟桂林府，有司歲時祀。

translations.literal: Thereupon the empress's father was enfeoffed as Duke of Qingyuan, special advancing Military Merit Minister, Special Promotion Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and Pillar of the State, with posthumous epithet Duanxi; her mother as Dame; a temple was established in Guilin Prefecture with seasonal sacrifices by the officials.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the empress's father was enfeoffed as Duke of Qingyuan, Special Promotion Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Pillar of the State, with the posthumous epithet Duanxi; her mother was made Dame; and a temple was established in Guilin Prefecture for annual sacrifice by the local officials.

sentences.zh: 大學士尹直撰哀冊有云：「睹漢家堯母之門，增宋室仁宗之慟。」

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Yin Zhi composed the lamentation text: "Seeing the gate of Yao's mother in the Han house, one adds to the Song emperor Renzong's grief."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Yin Zhi composed the lamentation text with the line: "To see the gate of Yao's mother in the Han house is to feel anew the grief of Emperor Renzong of Song."

sentences.zh: 帝燕閒念誦，輒欷歔流涕也。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor recited it in leisure moments, he would sigh and weep.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor recited it in private, he would sigh and weep.

sentences.zh: 孝惠邵太后，憲宗妃，興獻帝母也。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Xiaohui Shao was a consort of Xianzong and the mother of the Prince of Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Xiaohui Shao was a consort of Xianzong and mother of the Prince of Xing.

sentences.zh: 父林，昌化人，貧甚，鬻女於杭州鎮守太監，妃由此入宮。

translations.literal: Her father Lin was a native of Changhua, exceedingly poor; he sold his daughter to the eunuch commissioner at Hangzhou, and through this the consort entered the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Lin was from Changhua and desperately poor; he sold his daughter to the eunuch commissioner at Hangzhou, and through this she entered the palace.

sentences.zh: 知書，有容色。

translations.literal: She knew books and had a comely appearance.
translations.idiomatic: She was literate and beautiful.

sentences.zh: 成化十二年封宸妃，尋進封貴妃。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Chenghua she was enfeoffed as Honored Consort Chen; soon after she was advanced to honored consort.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Chenghua she was made Honored Consort Chen, and soon after was promoted to honored consort.

sentences.zh: 興王之籓，妃不得從。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Xing went to his fief, the consort could not accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Xing went to his fief, the consort was not permitted to follow.

sentences.zh: 世宗入繼大統，妃已老，目眚矣，喜孫為皇帝，摸世宗身，自頂至踵。

translations.literal: When Shizong succeeded to the great succession, the consort was already old and dim-sighted; delighted that her grandson had become emperor, she felt Shizong's body from crown to heel.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong succeeded to the throne, the consort was already old and blind; overjoyed that her grandson had become emperor, she felt Shizong's body from head to foot.

sentences.zh: 已，尊為皇太后。

translations.literal: Then she was honored as Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: She was then honored as Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖元年上尊號曰壽安。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiajing an exalted honorific was conferred: Shou An.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jiajing she was given the exalted honorific Shou An.

sentences.zh: 十一月崩。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month she died.
translations.idiomatic: She died in the eleventh month.

sentences.zh: 帝欲明年二月遷葬茂陵，大學士楊廷和等言：「祖陵不當數興工作，驚動神靈。」

translations.literal: The emperor wished to move her burial to Maoling in the second month of the following year; Grand Secretaries Yang Tinghe and others said: "The ancestral tombs should not repeatedly be disturbed with construction, startling the spirits."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to move her burial to Maoling in the second month of the following year; Grand Secretaries Yang Tinghe and others said, "The imperial tombs should not be repeatedly disturbed with new work, troubling the spirits."

sentences.zh: 不從。

translations.literal: He did not heed them.
translations.idiomatic: He did not listen.

sentences.zh: 諡曰「孝惠康肅溫仁懿順協天祐聖皇太后」，別祀奉慈殿。

translations.literal: Posthumous title: "Empress Dowager Xiaohui Kangsou Wenren Yishun Xietian Yousheng"; enshrined separately at the Hall of Filial Reverence.
translations.idiomatic: She was given the posthumous title "Empress Dowager Xiaohui Kangsou Wenren Yishun Xietian Yousheng" and enshrined separately in the Hall of Filial Reverence.

sentences.zh: 七年七月改稱太皇太后。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, seventh month, she was redesignated Grand Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the seventh year she was redesignated Grand Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 十五年遷主陵殿，稱皇后，與孝肅、孝穆等。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year her tablet was moved to the main tomb hall; she was titled Empress, alongside Xiaosu and Xiaomu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year her spirit tablet was moved to the main tomb hall and she was titled Empress, alongside Xiaosu and Xiaomu.

sentences.zh: 恭肅貴妃萬氏，諸城人。

translations.literal: Honored Consort Gongsu of the Wan clan was a native of Zhucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Honored Consort Gongsu of the Wan clan was from Zhucheng.

sentences.zh: 四歲選入掖廷，為孫太后宮女。

translations.literal: At four years old she was selected into the inner palace and became a handmaiden in Empress Dowager Sun's household.
translations.idiomatic: At the age of four she was selected for the inner palace and became a maid in Empress Dowager Sun's service.

sentences.zh: 及長，侍憲宗於東宮。

translations.literal: When she grew up she attended Xianzong in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When she grew up she attended Xianzong in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 憲宗年十六即位，妃已三十有五，機警，善迎帝意，遂讒廢皇后吳氏，六宮希得進禦。

translations.literal: Xianzong was sixteen when he ascended the throne; the consort was already thirty-five—shrewd, skilled at winning the emperor's favor; she slandered and brought about the deposition of Empress Wu, and throughout the six palaces few gained access to imperial favor.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong was sixteen when he took the throne; the consort was already thirty-five—clever and adept at pleasing the emperor. She slandered Empress Wu until she was deposed, and thereafter few women in the six palaces gained the emperor's favor.

sentences.zh: 帝每遊幸，妃戎服前驅。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor went on pleasure excursions, the consort went ahead in martial dress.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor went on excursions, the consort rode ahead in military dress.

sentences.zh: 成化二年正月生皇第一子，帝大喜，遣中使祀諸山川，遂封貴妃。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year of Chenghua she bore the emperor's first son; he was greatly pleased, sent palace envoys to sacrifice at mountains and rivers, and enfeoffed her as honored consort.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year of Chenghua she bore the emperor's first son; he was overjoyed, sent palace envoys to sacrifice at mountains and rivers, and made her an honored consort.

sentences.zh: 皇子未期薨，妃亦自是不復娠矣。

translations.literal: The prince died before completing his first year; the consort from then on also never conceived again.
translations.idiomatic: The prince died before his first birthday, and the consort never conceived again.

sentences.zh: 當是時，帝未有子，中外以為憂，言者每請溥恩澤以廣繼嗣。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor had no son; court and countryside were troubled, and memorialists repeatedly requested broadening grace to extend the succession.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the emperor still had no heir, and both court and realm were anxious; memorialists repeatedly urged him to extend grace and broaden the succession.

sentences.zh: 給事中李森、魏元，御史康永韶等先后言尤切。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretaries Li Sen and Wei Yuan, Censor Kang Yongshao, and others spoke in succession with particular urgency.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretaries Li Sen and Wei Yuan, Censor Kang Yongshao, and others spoke in turn with especial urgency.

sentences.zh: 四年秋，彗星屢見。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the fourth year comets appeared repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the fourth year comets appeared again and again.

sentences.zh: 大學士彭時、尚書姚夔亦以為言。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Peng Shi and Minister Yao Kui also spoke on the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Peng Shi and Minister Yao Kui also remonstrated on the same point.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「內事也，朕自主之。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "These are internal affairs—I decide them myself."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "These are palace matters—I shall decide them myself."

sentences.zh: 然不能用。

translations.literal: Yet he would not adopt their counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he would not heed them.

sentences.zh: 妃益驕。

translations.literal: The consort grew ever more arrogant.
translations.idiomatic: The consort grew ever more arrogant.

sentences.zh: 中官用事者，一忤意，立見斥逐。

translations.literal: Among eunuchs in power, whoever once offended her wishes was immediately dismissed and driven out.
translations.idiomatic: Any powerful eunuch who crossed her was summarily dismissed.

sentences.zh: 掖廷禦幸有身，飲藥傷墜者無數。

translations.literal: When women of the rear palace who had received the emperor's favor became pregnant, countless drank medicine to injure and miscarry.
translations.idiomatic: Countless women in the rear palace who became pregnant after imperial favor were forced to take abortifacients.

sentences.zh: 孝宗之生，頂寸許無發，或曰藥所中也。

translations.literal: When Xiaozong was born, on his crown there was about an inch without hair; some said it was from being struck by medicine.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozong was born, a patch on his crown about an inch across bore no hair—some said it was damage from abortifacients.

sentences.zh: 紀淑妃之死，實妃為之。

translations.literal: Consort Ji the Virtuous's death was in fact caused by the consort.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Ji the Virtuous was in fact killed at her instigation.

sentences.zh: 佞幸錢能、覃勤、汪直、梁芳、韋興輩皆假貢獻，苛斂民財，傾竭府庫，以結貴妃歡。

translations.literal: Favored sycophants Qian Neng, Tan Qin, Wang Zhi, Liang Fang, Wei Xing, and their like all used false tribute presentations, harshly levied the people's wealth, and drained the treasury to win the noble consort's favor.
translations.idiomatic: Favorites such as Qian Neng, Tan Qin, Wang Zhi, Liang Fang, and Wei Xing extorted the people and emptied the treasury under the guise of tribute to curry favor with her.

sentences.zh: 奇技淫巧，禱祠宮觀，糜費無算。

translations.literal: Strange skills and decadent crafts, prayers and sacrifices at palaces and shrines—waste without reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: Extravagant crafts, shrine-building, and ritual spending consumed untold sums.

sentences.zh: 久之，帝后宮生子漸多，芳等懼太子年長，他日立，將治己罪，同導妃勸帝易儲。

translations.literal: After a long time, sons born in the emperor's rear palace gradually increased; Fang and the others feared that when the crown prince grew older and was established one day, they would be punished for their crimes; together they guided the consort to urge the emperor to change the heir.
translations.idiomatic: In time, as more sons were born in the palace, Fang and his allies feared that once the grown crown prince succeeded he would punish them; they joined her in urging the emperor to replace the heir.

sentences.zh: 會泰山震，佔者謂應在東宮。

translations.literal: It happened that Mount Tai shook; diviners said the omen corresponded to the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Mount Tai shook, diviners said the omen pointed to the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 帝心懼，事乃寢。

translations.literal: The emperor's heart was afraid, and the matter thereupon was laid to rest.
translations.idiomatic: Frightened, the emperor dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 二十三年春，暴疾薨，帝輟朝七日。諡曰「恭肅端慎榮靖皇貴妃」，葬天壽山。弘治初，御史曹璘請削妃諡號；魚臺縣丞徐頊請逮治診視紀太后諸醫，捕萬氏家屬，究問當時薨狀。孝宗以重違先帝意，已之。

translations.literal: In the spring of the twenty-third year, she died of a sudden illness, and the emperor suspended court for seven days. Her posthumous title was "Reverent, Solemn, Upright, Careful, Honored, Tranquil Imperial Noble Consort," and she was buried at Tianshou Mountain. At the beginning of Hongzhi, Censor Cao Lin requested that the consort’s posthumous title be stripped; Xu Xu, assistant magistrate of Yutai County, requested that the physicians who had examined and treated Empress Dowager Ji be arrested and tried, that the Wan family relatives be arrested, and that the circumstances of her death at the time be investigated. Xiaozong, because he was reluctant to oppose the late emperor’s intent, stopped the matter.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the twenty-third year she died suddenly, and the emperor suspended court for seven days. She received the posthumous title "Reverent, Solemn, Upright, Careful, Honored, Tranquil Imperial Noble Consort" and was buried at Tianshou Mountain. At the beginning of Hongzhi, Censor Cao Lin asked that her posthumous title be stripped. Xu Xu, assistant magistrate of Yutai County, asked that the physicians who had examined and treated Empress Dowager Ji be arrested and tried, that the Wan family be arrested, and that the circumstances of Ji’s death be investigated. Xiaozong, reluctant to go against the late emperor’s wishes, stopped the matter.
